notes.title: Practice Set 1.1 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 1 Similarity
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 1.1 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 1.1 Chapter 1 Similarity Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 Base of a triangle is 9 and height is 5. Base of another triangle is 10 and height is 6. Find the ratio of areas of these triangles.

 Solution:

 Let the base, height and area of the first triangle be b 1, h 1, and A 1 respectively.

 Let the base, height and area of the second triangle be b 2, h 2 and A 2 respectively.

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-1.png?resize=209%2C204&ssl=1)

[Since Ratio of areas of two triangles is equal to the ratio of the product of their bases and corresponding heights]

 ∴ The ratio of areas of the triangles is 3:4.

Question 2.

 In the adjoining figure, BC ± AB, AD _L AB, BC = 4, AD = 8, then find A(Δ A B C)A(Δ A D B)

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-2.png?resize=182%2C185&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 ∆ABC and ∆ADB have same base AB.

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-3.png?resize=242%2C143&ssl=1)

 [Since Triangles having equal base]

Question 3.

 In the adjoining figure, seg PS ± seg RQ, seg QT ± seg PR. If RQ = 6, PS = 6 and PR = 12, then find QT.

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-4.png?resize=194%2C139&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆PQR, PR is the base and QT is the corresponding height.

 Also, RQ is the base and PS is the corresponding height.

A(Δ P Q R)A(Δ P Q R)=P R×Q T R Q×P S [Ratio of areas of two triangles is equal to the ratio of the product of their bases and corresponding heights]

 ∴ 1 1=P R×Q T R Q×P S

 ∴ PR × QT = RQ × PS

 ∴ 12 × QT = 6 × 6

 ∴ QT = 36 12

 ∴ QT = 3 units

Question 4.

 In the adjoining figure, AP ⊥ BC, AD || BC, then find A(∆ABC) : A(∆BCD).

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-5-1.png?resize=247%2C119&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Draw DQ ⊥ BC, B-C-Q.

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-6.png?resize=258%2C126&ssl=1)

 AD || BC [Given]

 ∴ AP = DQ(i) [Perpendicular distance between two parallel lines is the same]

 ∆ABC and ∆BCD have same base BC.

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-7.png?resize=573%2C142&ssl=1)

Question 5.

 In the adjoining figure, PQ ⊥ BC, AD ⊥ BC, then find following ratios.

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-8.png?resize=779%2C144&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 i. ∆PQB and tPBC have same height PQ.

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-9.png?resize=552%2C51&ssl=1)

 ii. ∆PBC and ∆ABC have same base BC.

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-10.png?resize=539%2C52&ssl=1)

 iii. ∆ABC and ∆ADC have same height AD.

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-11.png?resize=809%2C98&ssl=1)

Question 1.

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-12.png?resize=240%2C130&ssl=1)

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.1 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.1-13.png?resize=779%2C126&ssl=1)

notes.title: Practice Set 1.2 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 1 Similarity
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 1.2 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 1.2 Chapter 1 Similarity Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 Given below are some triangles and lengths of line segments. Identify in which figures, ray PM is the bisector of ∠QPR.

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-1.png?resize=799%2C176&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆ PQR,

P Q P R = 7 3 (i)

Q M R M = 3.5 1.5 = 35 15 = 7 3 (ii)

 ∴ P Q P R = Q M R M [From (i) and (ii)]

 ∴ Ray PM is the bisector of ∠QPR. [Converse of angle bisector theorem]

ii. In ∆PQR,

P Q P R = 10 7 (i)

Q M R M = 8 6 = 4 3 (ii)

 ∴ P Q P R ≠ Q M R M [From (i) and (ii)]

 ∴ Ray PM is not the bisector of ∠QPR

iii. In ∆PQR,

P Q P R = 9 10 (i)

Q M R M = 3.6 4 = 36 40 = 9 10 (ii)

 ∴ P Q P R = Q M R M [From (i) and (ii)]

 ∴ Ray PM is the bisector of ∠QPR [Converse of angle bisector theorem]

Question 2.

 In ∆PQR PM = 15, PQ = 25, PR = 20, NR = 8. State whether line NM is parallel to side RQ. Give reason.

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-2.png?resize=229%2C137&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 PN + NR = PR [P – N – R]

 ∴ PN + 8 = 20

 ∴ PN = 20 – 8 = 12

 Also, PM + MQ = PQ [P – M – Q]

 ∴ 15 + MQ = 25

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-3.png?resize=493%2C290&ssl=1)

 ∴ line NM || side RQ [Converse of basic proportionality theorem]

Question 3.

 In ∆MNP, NQ is a bisector of ∠N. If MN = 5, PN = 7, MQ = 2.5, then find QP.

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-4.png?resize=252%2C186&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆MNP, NQ is the bisector of ∠N. [Given]

 ∴P N M N = Q P M Q [Property of angle bisector of a triangle]

 ∴7 5 = Q P 2.5

 ∴ QP = 7×2.5 5

 ∴ QP = 3.5 units

Question 4.

 Measures of some angles in the figure are given. Prove that A P P B = A Q Q C

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-5.png?resize=188%2C130&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Proof

 ∠APQ = ∠ABC = 60° [Given]

 ∴ ∠APQ ≅ ∠ABC

 ∴ side PQ || side BC (i) [Corresponding angles test]

 In ∆ABC,

 sidePQ || sideBC [From (i)]

 ∴A P P B = A Q Q C [Basic proportionality theorem]

Question 5.

 In trapezium ABCD, side AB || side PQ || side DC, AP = 15, PD = 12, QC = 14, find BQ.

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-6.png?resize=218%2C102&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 side AB || side PQ || side DC [Given]

 ∴A P P D = B Q Q C [Property of three parallel lines and their transversals]

 ∴15 12 = B Q 14

 ∴ BQ = 15×14 12

 ∴ BQ = 17.5 units

Question 6.

 Find QP using given information in the figure.

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-7.png?resize=269%2C143&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆MNP, seg NQ bisects ∠N. [Given]

 ∴P N M N = Q P M Q [Property of angle bisector of a triangle]

 ∴40 25 = Q P 14

 ∴ QP = 40×14 25

 ∴ QP = 22.4 units

Question 7.

 In the adjoining figure, if AB || CD || FE, then find x and AE.

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-8.png?resize=217%2C114&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 line AB || line CD || line FE [Given]

 ∴B D D F = A C C E [Property of three parallel lines and their transversals]

 ∴8 4 = 12 X

 ∴ X = 12×4 8

 ∴ X = 6 units

 Now, AE AC + CE [A – C – E]

 = 12 + x

 = 12 + 6

 = 18 units

 ∴ x = 6 units and AE = 18 units

Question 8.

 In ∆LMN, ray MT bisects ∠LMN. If LM = 6, MN = 10, TN = 8, then find LT.

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-9.png?resize=281%2C122&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆LMN, ray MT bisects ∠LMN. [Given]

 ∴L M M N = L T T N [Property of angle bisector of a triangle]

 ∴6 10 = L T 8

 ∴ LT = 6×8 10

 ∴ LT = 4.8 units

Question 9.

 In ∆ABC,seg BD bisects ∠ABC. If AB = x,BC x+ 5, AD = x – 2, DC = x + 2, then find the value of x.

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-10.png?resize=274%2C127&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆ABC, seg BD bisects ∠ABC. [Given]

 ∴A B B C = A D C D [Property of angle bisector of a triangle]

 ∴x x+5 = x−2 x+2

 ∴ x(x + 2) = (x – 2)(x + 5)

 ∴ x2 + 2x = x2 + 5x – 2x – 10

 ∴ 2x = 3x – 10

 ∴ 10 = 3x – 2x

 ∴ x = 10

Question 10.

 In the adjoining figure, X is any point in the interior of triangle. Point X is joined to vertices of triangle. Seg PQ || seg DE, seg QR || seg EF. Fill in the blanks to prove that, seg PR || seg DF.

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-11.png?resize=273%2C164&ssl=1)

 Solution:

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-12.png?resize=667%2C269&ssl=1)

Question 11.

 In ∆ABC, ray BD bisects ∠ABC and ray CE bisects ∠ACB. If seg AB = seg AC, then prove that ED || BC.

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-13.png?resize=206%2C141&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆ABC, ray BD bisects ∠ABC. [Given]

 ∴A B B C = A E E B (i) [Property of angle bisector of a triangle]

 Also, in ∆ABC, ray CE bisects ∠ACB. [Given]

 ∴A C B C = A E E B (ii) [Property of angle bisector of a triangle]

 But, seg AB = seg AC (iii) [Given]

 ∴A B B C = A E E B (iv) [From (ii) and (iii)]

 ∴A D D C = A E E B [From (i) and (iv)]

 ∴ ED || BC [Converse of basic proportionality theorem]

Question 1.

 i. Draw a ∆ABC.

 ii. Bisect ∠B and name the point of intersection of AC and the angle bisector as D.

 iii. Measure the sides.

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-14.png?resize=203%2C59&ssl=1)

 iv. Find ratios A B B C and A D D C

 v. You will find that both the ratios are almost equal.

 vi. Bisect remaining angles of the triangle and find the ratios as above. Verify that the ratios are equal. (Textbook pg. no. 8)

 Solution:

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-15.png?resize=710%2C228&ssl=1)

 Note: Students should bisect the remaining angles and verify that the ratios are equal.

Question 2.

 Write another proof of the above theorem (property of an angle bisector of a triangle). Use the following properties and write the proof.

 i. The areas of two triangles of equal height are proportional to their bases.

 ii. Every point on the bisector of an angle is equidistant from the sides of the angle. (Textbook pg. no. 9)

![Image 18: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 16](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-16.png?resize=275%2C157&ssl=1)

 Given: In ∆CAB, ray AD bisects ∠A.

 To prove: A B A C = B D D C

 Construction: Draw seg DM ⊥ seg AB A – M – B and seg DN ⊥ seg AC, A – N – C.

 Solution:

 Proof:

 In ∆ABC,

 Point D is on angle bisector of ∠A. [Given]

 ∴DM = DN [Every point on the bisector of an angle is equidistant from the sides of the angle]

A(Δ A B D)A(Δ A C D)=A B×D M A C×D N [Ratio of areas of two triangles is equal to the ratio of the product of their bases and corresponding heights]

 ∴ A(Δ A B D)A(Δ A C D)=A B A C (ii) [From (i)]

 Also, ∆ABD and ∆ACD have equal height.

 ∴ A(Δ A B D)A(Δ A C D)=B D C D (iii) [Triangles having equal height]

 ∴A B A C=B D D C [From (ii) and (iii)]

Question 3.

 i. Draw three parallel lines.

 ii. Label them as l, m, n.

 iii. Draw transversals t 1 and t 2.

 iv. AB and BC are intercepts on transversal t 1.

 v. PQ and QR are intercepts on transversal t 2.

 vi. Find ratios A B B C and P Q Q R. You will find that they are almost equal. Verify that they are equal.(Textbook pg, no. 10)

 Solution:

![Image 19: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 17](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-17.png?resize=426%2C517&ssl=1)

 (Students should draw figures similar to the ones given and verify the properties.)

Question 4.

 In the adjoining figure, AB || CD || EF. If AC = 5.4, CE = 9, BD = 7.5, then find DF.(Textbook pg, no. 12)

![Image 20: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-18.png?resize=199%2C162&ssl=1)

 Solution:

![Image 21: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 19](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-19.png?resize=592%2C209&ssl=1)

Question 5.

 In ∆ABC, ray BD bisects ∠ABC. A – D – C, side DE || side BC, A – E – B, then prove that A B B C = A E E B (Textbook pg, no. 13)

![Image 22: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.2 20](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.2-20.png?resize=189%2C130&ssl=1)

notes.title: Practice Set 1.3 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 1 Similarity
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 1.3 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 1.3 Chapter 1 Similarity Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Practice Set 1.3 Question 1.

 In the adjoining figure, ∠ABC = 75°, ∠EDC = 75°. State which two triangles are similar and by which test? Also write the similarity of these two triangles by a proper one to one correspondence.

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-1.png?resize=174%2C166&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆ABC and ∆EDC,

 ∠ABC ≅ ∠EDC [Each angle is of measure 75°]

 ∠ACB ≅ ∠ECD [Common angle]

 ∴ ∆ABC ~ ∆EDC [AA test of similarity]

 One to one correspondence is

 ABC ↔ EDC

Similarity Class 10 Practice Set 1.3 Question 2.

 Are the triangles in the adjoining figure similar? If yes, by which test?

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-2.png?resize=316%2C142&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆PQR and ∆LMN,

P Q L M = 6 3 = 2 1 (i)

Q R M N = 8 4 = 2 1 (ii)

P R L N = 10 5 = 2 1 (iii)

 ∴ P Q L M = Q R M N = P R L N [From (i), (ii) and (iii)]

 ∴ ∆PQR – ∆LMN [SSS test of similarity]

Similarity Practice Set 1.3 Question 3.

 As shown in the adjoining figure, two poles of height 8 m and 4 m are perpendicular to the ground. If the length of shadow of smaller pole due to sunlight is 6 m, then how long will be the shadow of the bigger pole at the same time?

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-3.png?resize=319%2C130&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Here, AC and PR represents the bigger and smaller poles, and BC and QR represents their shadows respectively.

 Now, ∆ACB – ∆PRQ [ ∵ Vertical poles and their shadows form similar figures]

 ∴ C B R Q = A C P R [Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 ∴ x 6 = 8 4

 ∴ x=8×6 4

 ∴ x = 12 m

 ∴ The shadow of the bigger pole will be 12 metres long at that time.

Practice Set 1.3 Geometry 10th Maharashtra Board Question 4.

 In ∆ABC, AP ⊥ BC, BQ ⊥ AC, B – P – C, A – Q – C, then prove that ∆CPA – ∆CQB. If AP = 7, BQ = 8, BC = 12, then find AC.

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-4.png?resize=201%2C152&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆CPA and ∆CQB,

 ∠CPA ≅ ∠CQB [Each angle is of measure 90°]

 ∠ACP ≅ ∠BCQ [Common angle]

 ∴ ∆CPA ~ ∆CQB [AA test of similarity]

 ∴A C B C = A P B Q [Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 ∴ A C 12 = 7 8

 ∴ AC = x=12×7 8

 ∴ AC = 10.5 Units

10th Geometry Practice Set 1.3 Question 5.

 Given: In trapezium PQRS, side PQ || side SR, AR = 5 AP, AS = 5 AQ, then prove that SR = 5 PQ.

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-5.png?resize=193%2C133&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 side PQ || side SR [Given]

 and seg SQ is their transversal.

 ∴ ∠QSR = ∠SQP [Altemate angles]

 ∴ ∠ASR = ∠AQP (i) [Q – A – S]

 In ∆ASR and ∆AQP,

 ∠ASR = ∠AQP [From (i)]

 ∠SAR ≅ ∠QAP [Vertically opposite angles]

 ∆ASR ~ ∆AQP [AA test of similarity]

 ∴ A S A Q = S R P Q (ii) [Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 But, AS = 5 AQ [Given]

 ∴ A S A Q = 5 1 (iii)

 ∴ S R P Q = 5 1 [From (ii) and (iii)]

 ∴ SR = 5 PQ

Practice Set 1.3 Geometry 10th Question 6.

 Id trapezium ABCD (adjoining figure), side AB || side DC, diagonals AC and BD intersect in point O. If AB = 20, DC = 6, OB = 15, then find OD.

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-6.png?resize=238%2C147&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 side AB || side DC [Given]

 and seg BD is their transversal.

 ∴ ∠DBA ≅ ∠BDC [Alternate angles]

 ∴ ∠OBA ≅ ∠ODC (i) [D – O – B]

 In ∆OBA and ∆ODC

 ∠OBA ≅ ∠ODC [From (i)]

 ∠BOA ≅ ∠DOC [Vertically opposite angles]

 ∴ ∆OBA ~ ∆ODC [AA test of similarity]

 ∴ O B O D = A B D C [Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 ∴ 15 O D = 20 6

 ∴ OD = x=15×6 20

 ∴ OD = 4.5 units

Class 10 Geometry Practice Set 1.3 Question 7.

 ꠸ ABCD is a parallelogram. Point E is on side BC. Line DE intersects ray AB in point T. Prove that DE × BE = CE × TE.

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-7.png?resize=251%2C163&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Proof:

 ꠸ ABCD is a parallelogram. [Given]

 ∴ side AB || side CD [Opposite sides of a parallelogram]

 ∴ side AT || side CD [A – B – T]

 and seg DT is their transversal.

 ∴ ∠ATD ≅ ∠CDT [Alternate angles]

 ∴ ∠BTE ≅ ∠CDE (i) [A – B – T, T – E – D]

 In ∆BTE and ∆CDE,

 ∠BTE ≅ ∠CDE [From (i)]

 ∠BET ≅ ∠CED [Vertically opposite angles]

 ∴ ∆BTE ~ ∆CDE. [AA test of similarity]

 ∴ T E D E = B E C E [Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 ∴ DE × BE = CE × TE

Geometry Practice Set 1.3 Question 8.

 In the adjoining figure, seg AC and seg BD intersect each other in point P and A P C P = B P D P Prove that, ∆ABP ~ ∆CDP

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-8.png?resize=175%2C186&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Proof:

 In ∆ABP and ∆CDP,

A P C P = B P D P [Given]

 ∠APB ≅ ∠CPD [Vertically opposite angles]

 ∴ ∆ABP ~ ∆CDP [SAS test of similarity]

Math 2 Practice Set 1.3 Question 9.

 In the adjoining figure, in ∆ABC, point D is on side BC such that, ∠BAC = ∠ADC. Prove that, CA 2 = CB × CD,

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-9.png?resize=261%2C134&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Proof:

 In ∆BAC and ∆ADC,

 ∠BAC ≅ ∠ADC [Given]

 ∠BCA ≅ ∠ACD [Common angle]

 ∴ ∆BAC ~ ∆ADC [AA test of similarity]

 ∴ C A C D = C B C A [Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 ∴ CA × CA = CB × CD

 ∴ CA 2= CB × CD

Question 1.

 In the adjoining figure, BP ⊥ AC, CQ ⊥ AB, A – P – C, A – Q – B, then prove that ∆APB and ∆AQC are similar. (Textbook pg. no. 20)

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-10.png?resize=211%2C157&ssl=1)

 2. SAS test for similarity of triangles:

 For a given correspondence, if two pairs of corresponding sides are in the same proportion and the angle between them is congruent, then the two triangles are similar.

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-12.png?resize=328%2C137&ssl=1)

 In the given figure, if A B P Q = B C Q R, and ∠B ≅∠Q, then ∆ABC ~ ∆PQR

3. SSS test for similarity of triangles:

 For a given correspondence, if three sides of one triangle are in proportion with the corresponding three sides of the another triangle, then the two triangles are similar.

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Practice Set 1.3 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Practice-Set-1.3-13.png?resize=336%2C142&ssl=1)

 In the given figure, if A B P Q = B C Q R = A C P R, then ∆ABC ~ ∆PQR

Properties of similar triangles:

1.   Reflexivity: ∆ABC ~ ∆ABC
2.   Symmetry : If ∆ABC ~ ∆DEF, then ∆DEF ~ ∆ABC.
3.   Transitivity: If ∆ABC ~ ∆DEF and ∆DEF ~ ∆GHI, then ∆ABC ~ ∆GHI.

 Solution:

Question 4.

 ∆LMN ~ ∆PQR, 9 × A(∆PQR) = 16 × A(∆LMN). If QR = 20, then find MN.

 Solution:

 9 × A(∆PQR) = 16 × A(∆LMN) [Given]

 ∴ \frac{\mathrm{A}(\Delta \mathrm{LMN})}{\mathrm{A}(\Delta \mathrm{PQR})}=\frac{9}{16} (i)

 Now, ∆LMN ~ ∆PQR [Given]

 ∴ \frac{\mathrm{A}(\Delta \mathrm{LMN})}{\mathrm{A}(\Delta \mathrm{PQR})}=\frac{\mathrm{MN}^{2}}{\mathrm{QR}^{2}} (ii) [Theorem of areas of similar triangles]

 ∴ \frac{\mathrm{MN}^{2}}{\mathrm{QR}^{2}}=\frac{9}{16} [From (i) and (ii)]

 ∴ \frac{M N}{Q R}=\frac{3}{4} [Taking square root of both sides]

 ∴ \frac{\mathrm{MN}}{20}=\frac{3}{4}

 ∴ MN = \frac{20 \times 3}{4}

 ∴ MN = 15 units

Question 5.

 Areas of two similar triangles are 225 sq. cm. and 81 sq. cm. If a side of the smaller triangle is 12 cm, then find corresponding side of the bigger triangle.

 Solution:

 Let the areas of two similar triangles be A 1 and A 2.

 A 1 = 225 sq. cm. A 2 = 81 sq. cm.

 Let the corresponding sides of triangles be S 1 and S 2 respectively.

 S 1 = 12 cm

 ∴ The length of the corresponding side of the bigger triangle is 20 cm.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Problem Set 1 Chapter 1 Similarity Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 Select the appropriate alternative.

 i. In ∆ABC and ∆PQR, in a one to one correspondence A B Q R = B C P R = C A P Q, then

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-1.png?resize=302%2C124&ssl=1)

 (A) ∆PQR – ∆ABC

 (D) ∆BCA – ∆PQR

 Answer:

 (B)

ii. If in ∆DEF and ∆PQR, ∠D ≅ ∠Q, ∠R ≅ ∠E, then which of the following statements is false?

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-2.png?resize=319%2C134&ssl=1)

 (A) E F P R = D F P Q

 (B) D E P Q = E F R P

 (C) D E Q R = D F P Q

 (D) E F R P = D E Q R

 Answer:

 ∆DEF ~ ∆QRP … [AA test of similarity]

 ∴ D E Q R = E F R P = D F P Q …[Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 (B)

iii. In ∆ABC and ∆DEF, ∠B = ∠E, ∠F = ∠C and AB = 3 DE, then which of the statements regarding the two triangles is true?

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-3.png?resize=357%2C122&ssl=1)

 (A) The triangles are not congruent and not similar.

 (B) The triangles are similar but not congruent.

 (C) The triangles are congruent and similar.

 (D) None of the statements above is true.

 Answer:

 (B)

iv. ∆ABC and ∆DEF are equilateral triangles, A(∆ABC) : A(∆DEF) = 1 : 2. If AB = 4, then what is length of DE?

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-4.png?resize=300%2C152&ssl=1)

v. In the adjoining figure, seg XY || seg BC, then which of the following statements is true?

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-5.png?resize=207%2C123&ssl=1)

 (A) A B A C = A X A Y

 (B) A X X B = A Y A C

 (C) A X Y C = A Y X B

 (D) A B Y C = A C X B

 Answer:

 ∆ABC ~ ∆AXY … [AA test of similarity]

 ∴ A B A X = A C A Y …[Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 ∴ A B A C = A X A Y …[Altemendo]

 (A)

Question 2.

 In ∆ABC, B-D-C and BD = 7, BC = 20, then find following ratios.

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-6.png?resize=765%2C171&ssl=1)

 Solution:

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-7.png?resize=249%2C132&ssl=1)

 Draw AE ⊥ BC, B – E – C.

 BC = BD + DC [B – D – C]

 ∴ 20 = 7 + DC

 ∴ DC = 20 – 7 = 13

i. ∆ABD and ∆ADC have same height AE.

A(Δ A B D)A(Δ A D C)=B D D C [Triangles having equal height]

 ∴ A(Δ A B D)A(Δ A D C)=7 13

ii. ∆ABD and ∆ABC have same height AE.

A(Δ A B D)A(Δ A B C)=B D B C [Triangles having equal height]

 ∴ A(Δ A B D)A(Δ A B C)=7 20

iii. ∆ADC and ∆ABC have same height AE.

A(Δ A D C)A(Δ A B C)=D C B C [Triangles having equal height]

 ∴ A(Δ A D C)A(Δ A B C)=13 20

Question 3.

 Ratio of areas of two triangles with equal heights is 2 : 3. If base of the smaller triangle is 6 cm, then what is the corresponding base of the bigger triangle?

 Solution:

 Let A 1 and A 2 be the areas of two triangles. Let b 1 and b 2 be their corresponding bases.

 A 1 : A 2 = 2 : 3

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-8.png?resize=592%2C207&ssl=1)

∴ The corresponding base of the bigger triangle is 9 cm.

 In the adjoining figure, ∠ABC = ∠DCB = 90°, AB = 6, DC = 8, then A(Δ A B C)A(Δ D C B)=?

Question 5.

 In the adjoining figure, PM = 10 cm, A(∆PQS) = 100 sq. cm,

 A(∆QRS) = 110 sq. cm, then find NR.

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-11.png?resize=199%2C181&ssl=1)

 Solution:

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-12.png?resize=569%2C181&ssl=1)

 ∴ NR = 11 cm

Question 6.

 ∆MNT ~ ∆QRS. Length of altitude drawn from point T is 5 and length of altitude drawn from point S is 9. Find the ratio A(Δ M N T)A(Δ Q R S)

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-13.png?resize=290%2C137&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 ∆MNT- ∆QRS [Given]

 ∴ ∠M ≅ ∠Q (i) [Corresponding angles of similar triangles]

 In ∆MLT and ∆QPS,

 ∠M ≅ ∠Q [From (i)]

 ∠MLT ≅ ∠QPS [Each angle is of measure 90°]

 ∴ ∆MLT ~ ∆QPS [AA test of similarity]

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-14.png?resize=659%2C340&ssl=1)

Question 7.

 In the adjoining figure, A – D – C and B – E – C. seg DE || side AB. If AD = 5, DC = 3, BC = 6.4, then find BE.

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-15.png?resize=220%2C130&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆ABC,

 seg DE || side AB [Given]

 ∴ D C A D = E C B E [Basic proportionality theorem]

 ∴ 3 4 = 6.4−x x

 ∴ 3x = 5 (6.4 – x)

 ∴ 3x = 32 – 5x

 ∴ 8x = 32

 ∴ x = 32 8 =4

 ∴ BE = 4 units

Question 8.

 In the adjoining figure, seg PA, seg QB, seg RC and seg SD are perpendicular to line AD. AB = 60, BC = 70, CD = 80, PS = 280, then find PQ, QR and RS.

![Image 18: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 16](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-16.png?resize=175%2C171&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 seg PA, seg QB, seg RC and seg SD are perpendicular to line AD. [Given]

 ∴ seg PA || seg QB || seg RC || seg SD (i) [Lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel to each other]

 Let the value of PQ be x and that of QR be y.

 PS = PQ + QS [P – Q – S]

 ∴ 280 – x + QS

 ∴ QS = 280 – x (ii)

 Now, seg PA || seg QB || seg SD [From (i)]

 ∴ A B B D = P Q Q S [Property of three parallel lines and their transversals]

 ∴A B B C+C D = P Q Q S [B – C – D]

 ∴ 60 70+80 = x 280−x

 ∴ 60 150 = x 280−x

 ∴ 2 5 = x 280−x

 ∴ 5x = 2 (280 – x)

 ∴ 5x = 560 – 2x

 ∴ 7x = 560

 ∴ x = 560 7 = 80

 ∴ PQ = 80 units

 QS = 280 – x [From (ii)]

 = 280 – 80

 = 200 units

 But, QS = QR + RS [Q – R – S]

 ∴ 200 = y + RS

 ∴ RS = 200 – y (ii)

 Now, seg QB || seg RC || seg SD [From (i)]

 ∴B C C D = Q R R S [Property of three parallel lines and their transversals]

 ∴ 70 80 = y 200−y

 ∴ 7 8 = y 200−y

 ∴ 8y = 7(200 – y)

 ∴ 8y = 1400 – 7y

 ∴ 15y = 1400

 ∴ y = 1400 15 = 280 3

 ∴ QR = 280 3 units

 RS = 200 – 7 [From (iii)]

 = 200 – 280 3

 = 200×3−280 3

 = 600−280 3

 ∴ RS = 320 3 units

Question 9.

 In ∆PQR, seg PM is a median. Angle bisectors of ∠PMQ and ∠PMR intersect side PQ and side PR in points X and Y respectively. Prove that XY || QR

 Complete the proof by filling in the boxes.

![Image 19: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 17](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-17.png?resize=275%2C147&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Proof:

 In ∆PMQ, ray MX is bisector of ∠PMQ.

![Image 20: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-18.png?resize=686%2C251&ssl=1)

Question 10.

 In the adjoining figure, bisectors of ∠B and ∠C of ∆ABC intersect each other in point X. Line AX intersects side BC in point Y.

 AB = 5, AC = 4, BC = 6, then find A X X Y.

![Image 21: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 19](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-19.png?resize=222%2C211&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Let the value of BY be x.

 BC = BY + YC [B – Y – C]

 ∴ 6 = x + YC

 ∴ YC = 6 – x

 in ∆BAY, ray BX bisects ∠B. [Given]

 ∴ A B B Y = A X X Y (i) [Property of angle bisector of a triangle]

 Also, in ∆CAY, ray CX bisects ∠C. [Given]

![Image 22: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 20](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-20.png?resize=679%2C405&ssl=1)

Question 11.

 In ꠸ABCD, seg AD || seg BC. Diagonal AC and diagonal BD intersect each other in point P. Then show that A P P D = P C B P

![Image 23: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 21](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-21.png?resize=261%2C116&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 proof:

 seg AD || seg BC and BD is their transversal. [Given]

 ∴ ∠DBC ≅ ∠BDA [Alternate angles]

 ∴ ∠PBC ≅ ∠PDA (i) [D – P – B]

 In ∆PBC and ∆PDA,

 ∠PBC ≅ ∠PDA [From (i)]

 ∠BPC ≅ ∠DPA [Vertically opposite angles]

 ∴ ∆PBC ~ ∆PDA [AA test of similarity]

 ∴ B P P D = P C A P [Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 ∴ A P P D = P C B P [By altemendo]

Question 12.

 In the adjoining figure, XY || seg AC. If 2 AX = 3 BX and XY = 9, complete the activity to find the value of AC.

![Image 24: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 22](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-22.png?resize=216%2C131&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 2 AX = 3 BX [Given]

![Image 25: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 23](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-23.png?resize=504%2C155&ssl=1)![Image 26: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 24](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-24.png?resize=664%2C267&ssl=1)

Question 13.

 In the adjoining figure, the vertices of square DEFG are on the sides of ∆ABC. If ∠A = 90°, then prove that DE 2 = BD × EC.

 (Hint: Show that ∆GBD is similar to ∆ CFE. Use GD = FE = DE.)

![Image 27: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 25](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-25.png?resize=198%2C143&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 proof:

 ꠸DEFG is a square.

 ∴ DE = EF = GF = GD (i) [Sides of a square]

 ∠GDE = ∠DEF = 90° [Angles of a square]

 ∴ seg GD ⊥ side BC, seg FE ⊥ side BC (ii)

 In ∆BAC and ∆BDG,

 ∠BAC ≅ ∠BDG [From (ii), each angle is of measure 90°]

 ∠ABC ≅ ∠DBG [Common angle]

 ∴ ∆BAC – ∆BDG (iii) [AA test of similarity]

 In ∆BAC and ∆FEC,

 ∠BAC ≅ ∠FEC [From (ii), each angle is measure 90°]

 ∠ACB ≅ ∠ECF [Common angle]

 ∴ ∆BAC – ∆FEC (iv) [AA test of similarity]

 ∴ ∆BDG – ∆FEC [From (iii) and (iv)]

 ∴ B D E F = G D E C (v) [Corresponding sides of similar triangles]

 ∴ B D D E = D E E C [From (i) and (v)]

 ∴ DE 2 = BD × EC

notes.title: Practice Set 2.1 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 2.1 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 2.1 Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 Identify, with reason, which of the following are Pythagorean triplets.

 i. (3,5,4)

 ii. (4,9,12)

 iii. (5,12,13)

 iv. (24,70,74)

 v. (10,24,27)

 vi. (11,60,61)

 Solution:

 i. Here, 5 2 = 25

 3 2 + 4 2 = 9 + 16 = 25

 ∴ 5 2 = 3 2 + 4 2

 The square of the largest number is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ (3,5,4) is a Pythagorean triplet.

ii. Here, 12 2 = 144

 4 2 + 9 2= 16 + 81 =97

 ∴ 12 2 ≠ 4 2 + 92

 The square of the largest number is not equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ (4,9,12) is not a Pythagorean triplet.

iii. Here, 13 2 = 169

 5 2 + 12 2 = 25 + 144 = 169

 ∴ 13 2 = 5 2 + 12 2

 The square of the largest number is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ (5,12,13) is a Pythagorean triplet.

iv. Here, 74 2 = 5476

 24 2 + 70 2 = 576 + 4900 = 5476

 ∴ 74 2 = 24 2 + 70 2

 The square of the largest number is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ (24, 70,74) is a Pythagorean triplet.

v. Here, 27 2 = 729

 10 2 + 24 2 = 100 + 576 = 676

 ∴ 27 2 ≠ 10 2 + 24 2

 The square of the largest number is not equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ (10,24,27) is not a Pythagorean triplet.

vi. Here, 61 2 = 3721

 11 2 + 60 2 = 121 + 3600 = 3721

 ∴ 61 2 = 11 2 + 60 2

 The square of the largest number is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ (11,60,61) is a Pythagorean triplet.

Question 2.

 In the adjoining figure, ∠MNP = 90°, seg NQ ⊥ seg MP,MQ = 9, QP = 4, find NQ.

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 1 Similarity Problem Set 1 25](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-1-Similarity-Problem-Set-1-25-1.png?resize=198%2C143&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆MNP, ∠MNP = 90° and [Given]

 seg NQ ⊥ seg MP

 NQ 2 = MQ × QP [Theorem of geometric mean]

 ∴ NQ = M Q×Q P−−−−−−−−−√ [Taking square root of both sides]

 = 9×4−−−−√

 = 3 × 2

 ∴NQ = 6 units

Question 3.

 In the adjoining figure, ∠QPR = 90°, seg PM ⊥ seg QR and Q – M – R, PM = 10, QM = 8, find QR.

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-2.png?resize=203%2C134&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆PQR, ∠QPR = 90° and [Given]

 seg PM ⊥ seg QR

 ∴ PM 2 = OM × MR [Theorem of geometric mean]

 ∴ 10 2 = 8 × MR

 ∴ MR = 100 8

 = 12.5

 Now, QR = QM + MR [Q – M – R]

 = 8 + 12.5

 ∴ QR = 20.5 units

Question 4.

 See adjoining figure. Find RP and PS using the information given in ∆PSR.

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-3.png?resize=208%2C129&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆PSR, ∠S = 90°, ∠P = 30° [Given]

 ∴ ∠R = 60° [Remaining angle of a triangle]

 ∴ ∆PSR is a 30° – 60° – 90° triangle.

 RS = 1 2 RP [Side opposite to 30°]

 ∴6 = 1 2 RP

 ∴ RP = 6 × 2 = 12 units

 Also, PS = 3√2 RP [Side opposite to 60°]

 = 3√2 × 12

 = 6 3–√ units

 ∴ RP = 12 units, PS = 6 3–√ units

Question 5.

 For finding AB and BC with the help of information given in the adjoining figure, complete the following activity.

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-4.png?resize=165%2C151&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 AB = BC [Given]

 ∴ ∠BAC = ∠BCA [Isosceles triangle theorem]

 Let ∠BAC = ∠BCA = x (i)

 In ∆ABC, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180° [Sum of the measures of the angles of a triangle is 180°]

 ∴ x + 90° + x = 180° [From (i)]

 ∴ 2x = 90°

 ∴ x = 90°2 [From (i)]

 ∴ x = 45°

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-5.jpg?resize=518%2C202&ssl=1)

Question 6.

 Find the side and perimeter of a square whose diagonal is 10 cm.

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-11.jpg?resize=143%2C127&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Let ꠸ABCD be the given square.

 l(diagonal AC) = 10 cm

 Let the side of the square be ‘x’ cm.

 In ∆ABC,

 ∠B = 90° [Angle of a square]

 ∴ AC 2 = AB 2 + BC 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ 10 2 = x 2 + x 2

 ∴ 100 = 2x 2

 ∴ x 2 = 100 2

 ∴x 2 = 50

 ∴ x = 50−−√ [Taking square root of both sides]

 = =25×2−−−−−√=5 2–√

 ∴side of square is 5 2–√ cm.

 = 4 × 5 2–√

 ∴ Perimeter of square = 20 2–√ cm

Question 7.

 In the adjoining figure, ∠DFE = 90°, FG ⊥ ED. If GD = 8, FG = 12, find

 i. EG

 ii. FD, and

 iii. EF

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-6.png?resize=207%2C107&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 i. In ∆DEF, ∠DFE = 90° and FG ⊥ ED [Given]

 ∴ FG 2 = GD × EG [Theorem of geometric mean]

 ∴ 122 = 8 × EG .

 ∴ EG = 144 8

 ∴ EG = 18 units

ii. In ∆FGD, ∠FGD = 90° [Given]

 ∴ FD 2 = FG 2 + GD 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 = 122 + 82 = 144 + 64

 = 208

 ∴ FD = 208−−−√ [Taking square root of both sides]

 ∴ FD = 4 13−−√ units

iii. In ∆EGF, ∠EGF = 90° [Given]

 ∴ EF 2 = EG 2 + FG 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 = 182 + 122 = 324 + 144

 = 468

 ∴ EF = 468−−−√ [Taking square root of both sides]

 ∴ EF = 6 13−−√ units

Question 8.

 Find the diagonal of a rectangle whose length is 35 cm and breadth is 12 cm.

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-7.png?resize=227%2C105&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Let ꠸ABCD be the given rectangle.

 AB = 12 cm, BC 35 cm

 In ∆ABC, ∠B = 90° [Angle of a rectangle]

 ∴ AC 2 = AB 2 + BC 2[Pythagoras theorem]

 = 122 + 352

 = 144 + 1225

 = 1369

 ∴ AC = 1369−−−−√ [Taking square root of both sides]

 = 37 cm

 ∴ The diagonal of the rectangle is 37 cm.

Question 9.

 In the adjoining figure, M is the midpoint of QR. ∠PRQ = 90°.

 Prove that, PQ 2 = 4 PM 2 – 3 PR 2.

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-8.png?resize=217%2C135&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 Proof:

 In ∆PQR, ∠PRQ = 90° [Given]

 PQ 2 = PR 2 + QR 2 (i) [Pythagoras theorem]

 RM = 1 2 QR [M is the midpoint of QR]

 ∴ 2RM = QR (ii)

 ∴ PQ 2 = PR 2 + (2RM)2 [From (i) and (ii)]

 ∴ PQ 2 = PR 2 + 4RM 2 (iii)

 Now, in ∆PRM, ∠PRM = 90° [Given]

 ∴ PM 2 = PR 2 + RM 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ RM 2 = PM 2 – PR 2 (iv)

 ∴ PQ 2 = PR 2 + 4 (PM 2 – PR 2) [From (iii) and (iv)]

 ∴ PQ 2 = PR 2 + 4 PM 2 – 4 PR 2

 ∴ PQ 2 = 4 PM 2 – 3 PR 2

Question 10.

 Walls of two buildings on either side of a street are parallel to each other. A ladder 5.8 m long is placed on the street such that its top just reaches the window of a building at the height of 4 m. On turning the ladder over to the other side of the street, its top touches the window of the other building at a height 4.2 m. Find the width of the street.

 Solution:

 Let AC and CE represent the ladder of length 5.8 m, and A and E represent windows of the buildings on the opposite sides of the street. BD is the width of the street.

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-9.png?resize=325%2C135&ssl=1)

 AB = 4 m and ED = 4.2 m

 In ∆ABC, ∠B = 90° [Given]

 AC 2 = AB 2 + BC 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ 5.8 2 = 4 2 + BC 2

 ∴ 5.8 2 – 4 2 = BC 2

 ∴ (5.8 – 4) (5.8 + 4) = BC 2

 ∴ 1.8 × 9.8 = BC 2

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.1-10.jpg?resize=598%2C235&ssl=1)

 CE 2 = CD 2 + DE 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ 5.8 2 = CD 2 + 4.22

 ∴ 5.8 2 – 4.2 2 = CD 2

 ∴ (5.8 – 4.2) (5.8 + 4.2) = CD 2

 ∴ 1.6 × 10 = CD 2

 ∴ CD 2 = 16

 ∴ CD = 4m (ii) [Taking square root of both sides]

 Now, BD = BC + CD [B – C – D]

 = 4.2 + 4 [From (i) and (ii)]

 = 8.2 m

 ∴ The width of the street is 8.2 metres.

Question 1.

 Verify that (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), (24,25,7) are Pythagorean triplets. (Textbook pg. no. 30)

 Solution:

 i. Here, 5 2 = 25

 3 2 + 4 2 = 9 + 16 = 25

 ∴ 5 2 = 3 2 + 4 2

 The square of the largest number is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ 3,4,5 is a Pythagorean triplet.

ii. Here, 13 2 = 169

 5 2 + 12 2 = 25 + 144 = 169

 ∴ 13 2 = 5 2 + 12 2

 The square of the largest number is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ 5,12,13 is a Pythagorean triplet.

iii. Here, 17 2 = 289

 8 2 + 15 2 = 64 + 225 = 289

 ∴ 17 2 = 8 2 + 15 2

 The square of the largest number is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ 8,15,17 is a Pythagorean triplet.

iv. Here, 25 2 = 625

 7 2 + 24 2 = 49 + 576 = 625

 ∴ 25 2 = 7 2 + 24 2

 The square of the largest number is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two numbers.

 ∴ 24,25, 7 is a Pythagorean triplet.

Question 2.

 Assign different values to a and b and obtain 5 Pythagorean triplets. (Textbook pg. no. 31)

 Solution:

 i. Let a = 2, b = 1

 a 2 + b 2 = 2 2 + 1 2 = 4 + 1 = 5

 a 2 – b 2 = 2 2 – 1 2 = 4 – 1 = 3

 2ab = 2 × 2 × 1 = 4

 ∴ (5, 3, 4) is a Pythagorean triplet.

ii. Let a = 4,b = 3

 a 2 + b 2 = 4 2 + 3 2 = 16 + 9 = 25

 a 2 – b 2 = 4 2 – 3 2 = 16 – 9 = 7

 2ab = 2 × 4 × 3 = 24

 ∴ (25, 7, 24) is a Pythagorean triplet.

iii. Let a = 5, b = 2

 a 2 + b 2 = 5 2 + 2 2 = 25 + 4 = 29

 a 2 – b 2 = 5 2 – 2 2 = 25 – 4 = 21

 2ab = 2 × 5 × 2 = 20

 ∴ (29, 21, 20) is a Pythagorean triplet.

iv. Let a = 4,b = 1

 a 2 + b 2 = 4 2 + 1 2 = 16 + 1 = 17

 a 2 – b 2 = 42 – 12 = 16 – 1 = 15

 2ab = 2 × 4 × 1 = 8

 ∴ (17, 15, 8) is a Pythagorean triplet.

v. Let a = 9, b = 7

 a 2 + b 2 = 92 + 72 = 81 + 49 = 130

 a 2 – b 2 = 92 – 72 = 81 – 49 = 32

 2ab = 2 × 9 × 7 = 126

 ∴ (130,32,126) is a Pythagorean triplet.

Note: Numbers in Pythagorean triplet can be written in any order.

notes.title: Practice Set 2.2 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 2.2 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 2.2 Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 In ∆PQR, point S is the midpoint of side QR. If PQ = 11, PR = 17, PS = 13, find QR.

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-1.png?resize=179%2C140&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆PQR, point S is the midpoint of side QR. [Given]

 ∴ seg PS is the median.

 ∴ PQ 2 + PR 2 = 2 PS 2 + 2 SR 2 [Apollonius theorem]

 ∴ 11 2 + 17 2 = 2 (13)2 + 2 SR 2

 ∴ 121 + 289 = 2 (169)+ 2 SR 2

 ∴ 410 = 338+ 2 SR 2

 ∴ 2 SR 2 = 410 – 338

 ∴ 2 SR 2 = 72

 ∴ SR 2 = 72 2 = 36

 ∴ SR = 36−−√ [Taking square root of both sides]

 = 6 units Now, QR = 2 SR [S is the midpoint of QR]

 = 2 × 6

 ∴ QR = 12 units

Question 2.

 In ∆ABC, AB = 10, AC = 7, BC = 9, then find the length of the median drawn from point C to side AB.

 Solution:

 Let CD be the median drawn from the vertex C to side AB.

 BD = 1 2 AB [D is the midpoint of AB]

 = 1 2 × 10 = 5 units

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-2.png?resize=184%2C149&ssl=1)

 In ∆ABC, seg CD is the median. [Given]

 ∴ AC 2 + BC 2 = 2 CD 2 + 2 BD 2 [Apollonius theorem]

 ∴ 7 2 + 9 2 = 2 CD 2 + 2 (5)2

 ∴ 49 + 81 = 2 CD 2 + 2 (25)

 ∴ 130 = 2 CD 2 + 50

 ∴ 2 CD 2 = 130 – 50

 ∴ 2 CD 2 = 80

 ∴ CD 2 = 80 2 = 40

 ∴ CD = 40−−√ [Taking square root of both sides]

 = 2 10−−√ units

 ∴ The length of the median drawn from point C to side AB is 2 10−−√ units.

Question 3.

 In the adjoining figure, seg PS is the median of APQR and PT ⊥ QR. Prove that,

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-3.png?resize=202%2C156&ssl=1)

 i. PR 2 = PS 2 + QR × ST + (Q R 2)2

 ii. PQ 2 = PS 2 – QR × ST + (Q R 2)2

 Solution:

 i. QS = SR = 1 2 QR (i) [S is the midpoint of side QR]

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-4.png?resize=176%2C153&ssl=1)

 ∴ In ∆PSR, ∠PSR is an obtuse angle [Given]

 and PT ⊥ SR [Given, Q-S-R]

 ∴ PR 2 = SR 2 +PS 2 + 2 SR × ST (ii) [Application of Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ PR 2 = (1 2 QR)2 + PS 2 + 2 (1 2 QR) × ST [From (i) and (ii)]

 ∴ PR 2 = (Q R 2)2 + PS 2 + QR × ST

 ∴ PR 2 = PS 2 + QR × ST + (Q R 2)2

ii. In.∆PQS, ∠PSQ is an acute angle and [Given]

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-5.png?resize=134%2C158&ssl=1)

 PT ⊥QS [Given, Q-S-R]

 ∴ PQ 2 = QS 2 + PS 2 – 2 QS × ST (iii) [Application of Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ PR 2 = (1 2 QR)2 + PS 2 – 2 (1 2 QR) × ST [From (i) and (iii)]

 ∴ PR 2 = (Q R 2)2 + PS 2 – QR × ST

 ∴ PR 2 = PS 2 – QR × ST + (Q R 2)2

Question 4.

 In ∆ABC, point M is the midpoint of side BC. If AB 2 + AC 2 = 290 cm, AM = 8 cm, find BC.

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-6.png?resize=149%2C134&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆ABC, point M is the midpoint of side BC. [Given]

 ∴ seg AM is the median.

 ∴ AB 2 + AC 2 = 2 AM 2 + 2 MC 2 [Apollonius theorem]

 ∴ 290 = 2 (8)2 + 2 MC 2

 ∴ 145 = 64 + MC 2 [Dividing both sides by 2]

 ∴ MC 2 = 145 – 64

 ∴ MC 2 = 81

 ∴ MC = 81−−√ [Taking square root of both sides]

 MC = 9 cm

 Now, BC = 2 MC [M is the midpoint of BC]

 = 2 × 9

 ∴ BC = 18 cm

Question 5.

 In the adjoining figure, point T is in the interior of rectangle PQRS. Prove that, TS 2 + TQ 2 = TP 2 + TR 2. (As shown in the figure, draw seg AB || side SR and A – T – B)

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-14.jpg?resize=237%2C117&ssl=1)

 Given: ꠸PQRS is a rectangle.

 Point T is in the interior of ꠸PQRS.

 To prove: TS 2 + TQ 2 = TP 2 + TR 2

 Construction: Draw seg AB || side SR such that A – T – B.

 Solution:

 Proof:

 ꠸PQRS is a rectangle. [Given]

 ∴ PS = QR (i) [Opposite sides of a rectangle]

 In ꠸ASRB,

 ∠S = ∠R = 90° (ii) [Angles of rectangle PQRS]

 side AB || side SR [Construction]

 Also ∠A = ∠S = 90° [Interior angle theorem, from (ii)]

 ∠B = ∠R = 90°

 ∴ ∠A = ∠B = ∠S = ∠R = 90° (iii)

 ∴ ꠸ASRB is a rectangle.

 ∴ AS = BR (iv) [Opposite sides of a rectanglel

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-1.jpg?resize=104%2C126&ssl=1)

 In ∆PTS, ∠PST is an acute angle

 and seg AT ⊥ side PS [From (iii)]

 ∴ TP 2 = PS 2 + TS 2– 2 PS.AS (v) [Application of Pythagoras theorem]

 In ∆TQR., ∠TRQ is an acute angle

 and seg BT ⊥ side QR [From (iii)]

 ∴ TQ 2 = RQ 2 + TR 2 – 2 RQ.BR (vi) [Application of pythagoras theorem]

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-2.jpg?resize=151%2C110&ssl=1)

 TP 2 – TQ 2 = PS 2 + TS 2 – 2PS.AS

 -RQ 2 – TR 2 + 2RQ.BR [Subtracting (vi) from (v)]

 ∴ TP 2 – TQ 2 = TS 2 – TR 2 + PS 2

 – RQ 2 -2 PS.AS +2 RQ.BR

 ∴ TP 2 – TQ 2 = TS 2 – TR 2 + PS 2

 – PS 2 – 2 PS.BR + 2PS.BR [From (i) and (iv)]

 ∴ TP 2 – TQ 2 = TS 2 – TR 2

 ∴ TS 2 + TQ 2 = TP 2 + TR 2

Question 1.

 In ∆ABC, ∠C is an acute angle, seg AD Iseg BC. Prove that: AB 2 = BC 2 + A 2 – 2 BC × DC. (Textbook pg. no. 44)

 Given: ∠C is an acute angle, seg AD ⊥ seg BC.

 To prove: AB 2 = BC 2 + AC 2 – 2BC × DC

 Solution:

 Proof:

 ∴ LetAB = c, AC = b, AD = p,

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-9.png?resize=208%2C170&ssl=1)

 ∴ BC = a, DC = x

 BD + DC = BC [B – D – C]

 ∴ BD = BC – DC

 ∴ BD = a – x

 In ∆ABD, ∠D = 90° [Given]

 AB 2 = BD 2 + AD 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ c 2 = (a – x)2 + [P 2] (i)

 ∴ c 2 = a 2 – 2ax + x 2 + [P 2]

 In ∆ADC, ∠D = 90° [Given]

 AC 2 = AD 2 + CD 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ b 2 = p 2 + [X 2]

 ∴ p 2 = b 2 – [X 2] (ii)

 ∴ c 2 = a 2 – 2ax + x 2 + b 2 – x 2 [Substituting (ii) in (i)]

 ∴ c 2 = a 2 + b 2 – 2ax

 ∴ AB 2 = BC 2 + AC 2 – 2 BC × DC

Question 2.

 In ∆ABC, ∠ACB is an obtuse angle, seg AD ⊥ seg BC. Prove that: AB 2 = BC 2 + AC 2 + 2 BC × CD. (Textbook pg. no. 40 and 4.1)

 Given: ∠ACB is an obtuse angle, seg AD ⊥ seg BC.

 To prove: AB 2 = BC 2 + AC 2 + 2BC × CD

 Solution:

 Proof:

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-10.png?resize=264%2C139&ssl=1)

 Let AD = p, AC = b, AB = c,

 BC = a, DC = x

 BD = BC + DC [B – C – D]

 ∴ BD = a + x

 In ∆ADB, ∠D = 90° [Given]

 AB 2 = BD 2 + AD 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ c 2 = (a + x)2 + p 2 (i)

 ∴ c 2 = a 2 + 2ax + x 2 + p 2

 Also, in ∆ADC, ∠D = 90° [Given]

 AC 2 = CD 2 + AD 2 [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ b 2 = x 2 + p 2

 ∴ p 2 = b 2 – x 2 (ii)

 ∴ c 2 = a 2 + 2ax + x 2 + b 2 – x 2 [Substituting (ii) in (i)]

 ∴ c 2 = a 2 + b 2 + 2ax

 ∴ AB 2 = BC 2 + AC 2 + 2 BC × CD

Question 3.

 In ∆ABC, if M is the midpoint of side BC and seg AM ⊥seg BC, then prove that

 AB 2 + AC 2 = 2 AM 2 + 2 BM 2. (Textbook pg, no. 41)

 Given: In ∆ABC, M is the midpoint of side BC and seg AM ⊥ seg BC.

 To prove: AB 2 + AC 2 = 2 AM 2 + 2 BM 2

 Solution:

 Proof:

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 2 Pythagoras Theorem Practice Set 2.2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-2-Pythagoras-Theorem-Practice-Set-2.2-3.jpg?resize=192%2C169&ssl=1)

 In ∆AMB, ∠M = 90° [segAM ⊥ segBC]

 ∴ AB2 = AM2 + BM2 (i) [Pythagoras theorem]

 Also, in ∆AMC, ∠M = 90° [seg AM ⊥ seg BC]

 ∴ AC2 = AM2 + MC2 (ii) [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ AB 2 + AC 2 = AM 2 + BM 2 + AM 2 + MC 2 [Adding (i) and (ii)]

 ∴ AB 2 + AC 2 = 2 AM 2 + BM 2 + BM 2 [∵ BM = MC (M is the midpoint of BC)]

 ∴ AB 2 + AC 2 = 2 AM 2 + 2 BM 2
