notes.title: Practice Set 5.1 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 5.1 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 5.1 Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Practice Set 5.1 Geometry Class 10 Question 1. Find the distance between each of the following pairs of points.

 i. A (2, 3), B (4,1)

 ii. P (-5, 7), Q (-1, 3)

 iii. R (0, -3), S (0,5 2)

 iv. L (5, -8), M (-7, -3)

 v. T (-3, 6), R (9, -10)

 vi. W(−7 2,4), X(11, 4)

 Solution:

 i. Let A (x 1, y 1) and B (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 ∴ x 1 = 2, y 1 = 3, x 2 = 4, y 2 = 1

 By distance formula,

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-3.png?resize=299%2C90&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(A, B) = 2 2–√ units

 ∴ The distance between the points A and B is 2 2–√ units.

ii. Let P (x 1, y 1 ) and Q (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 ∴ x 1 = -5, y 1 = 7, x 2 = -1, y 2 = 3

 By distance formula,

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-1.png?resize=285%2C192&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(P, Q) = 4 2–√ units

 ∴ The distance between the points P and Q is 4 2–√ units.

iii. Let R (x 1, y 1) and S (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 ∴ x 1 = 0, y 1 = -3, x 2 = 0, y 2 = 5 2

 By distance formula,

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-2.png?resize=310%2C307&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(R, S) = 11 2 units

 ∴ The distance between the points R and S is 11 2 units.

iv. Let L (x 1, y 1) and M (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 ∴ x 1 = 5, y 1 = -8, x 2 = -7, y 2 = -3

 By distance formula,

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-4.png?resize=267%2C187&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(L, M) = 13 units

 ∴ The distance between the points L and M is 13 units.

v. Let T (x 1,y 1) and R (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 ∴ x 1 = -3, y 1 = 6,x 2 = 9,y 2 = -10

 By distance formula,

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-5.png?resize=247%2C182&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(T, R) = 20 units

 ∴ The distance between the points T and R 20 units.

vi. Let W (x 1, y 1) and X (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-6.png?resize=250%2C316&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(W, X) = 29 2 units

 ∴ The distance between the points W and X is 29 2 units.

Practice Set 5.1 Geometry 10th Question 2. Determine whether the points are collinear.

 i. A (1, -3), B (2, -5), C (-4, 7)

 ii. L (-2, 3), M (1, -3), N (5, 4)

 iii. R (0, 3), D (2, 1), S (3, -1)

 iv. P (-2, 3), Q (1, 2), R (4, 1)

 Solution:

 i. By distance formula,

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-7.png?resize=269%2C186&ssl=1)

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-8.png?resize=328%2C370&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(A, B) = 5–√ …(i)

 On adding (i) and (iii),

 d(A, B) + d(A, C)= 5–√ + 5 5–√ = 6 5–√

 ∴ d(A, B) + d(A, C) = d(B, C) … [From (ii)]

 ∴ Points A, B and C are collinear.

ii. By distance formula,

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-9.jpg?resize=325%2C556&ssl=1)

 On adding (i) and (iii),

 d(L, M) + d(L, N) = 3 5–√ + 5 2–√ ≠ 65−−√

 ∴ d(L, M) + d(L, N) ≠ d(M, N) … [From (ii)]

 ∴ Points L, M and N are not collinear.

iii. By distance formula,

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-10.png?resize=328%2C450&ssl=1)

 On adding (i) and (ii),

 ∴ d(R, D) + d(D, S) = 8–√ + 5–√ ≠ 5

 ∴ d(R, D) + d(D, S) ≠ d(R, S) … [From (iii)]

 ∴ Points R, D and S are not collinear.

iv. By distance formula,

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-11.png?resize=324%2C551&ssl=1)

 On adding (i) and (ii),

 d(P, Q) + d(Q, R) = 10−−√ + 10−−√ = 2 10−−√

 ∴ d(P, Q) + d(Q, R) = d(P, R) … [From (iii)]

 ∴ Points P, Q and R are collinear.

Coordinate Geometry Class 10 Practice Set 5.1 Question 3. Find the point on the X-axis which is equidistant from A (-3,4) and B (1, -4).

 Solution:

 Let point C be on the X-axis which is equidistant from points A and B.

 Point C lies on X-axis.

 ∴ its y co-ordinate is 0.

 Let C = (x, 0)

 C is equidistant from points A and B.

 ∴ AC = BC

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-12.png?resize=337%2C100&ssl=1)

 ∴ (x + 3)2 + (-4)2 = (x- 1)2 + 4 2

 ∴ x 2 + 6x + 9 + 16 = x 2 – 2x + 1 + 16

 ∴ 8x = – 8

 ∴ x = – 8 8 = -1

 ∴ The point on X-axis which is equidistant from points A and B is (-1,0).

10th Geometry Practice Set 5.1 Question 4. Verify that points P (-2, 2), Q (2, 2) and R (2, 7) are vertices of a right angled triangle.

 Solution:

 Distance between two points

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-13.png?resize=338%2C314&ssl=1)

 Consider, PQ 2 + QR 2 = 42 + 52 = 16 + 25 = 41 … [From (i) and (ii)]

 ∴ PR 2 = PQ 2 + QR 2 … [From (iii)]

 ∴ ∆PQR is a right angled triangle. … [Converse of Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ Points P, Q and R are the vertices of a right angled triangle.

Question 5.

 Show that points P (2, -2), Q (7, 3), R (11, -1) and S (6, -6) are vertices of a parallelogram.

 Proof:

 Distance between two points

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-14.png?resize=338%2C433&ssl=1)

 PQ = RS … [From (i) and (iii)]

 QR = PS … [From (ii) and (iv)]

 A quadrilateral is a parallelogram, if both the pairs of its opposite sides are congruent.

 ∴ □ PQRS is a parallelogram.

 ∴ Points P, Q, R and S are the vertices of a parallelogram.

Question 6.

 Show that points A (-4, -7), B (-1, 2), C (8, 5) and D (5, -4) are vertices of rhombus ABCD.

 Proof:

 Distance between two points

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-15.png?resize=345%2C330&ssl=1)

![Image 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-16.png?resize=341%2C105&ssl=1)

 ∴ AB = BC = CD = AD …[From (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)]

 In a quadrilateral, if all the sides are equal, then it is a rhombus.

 ∴ □ ABCD is a rhombus.

 ∴ Points A, B, C and D are the vertices of rhombus ABCD.

Practice Set 5.1 Question 7. Find x if distance between points L (x, 7) and M (1,15) is 10.

 Solution:

 X 1 = x, y 1 = 7, x 2 = 1, y 2 = 15

 By distance formula,

![Image 19: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 17](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-17.png?resize=384%2C217&ssl=1)

 ∴ 1 – x = ± 6

 ∴ 1 – x = 6 or l – x = -6

 ∴ x = – 5 or x = 7

 ∴ The value of x is – 5 or 7.

Geometry 5.1 Question 8. Show that the points A (1, 2), B (1, 6), C (1 + 2 3–√, 4) are vertices of an equilateral triangle.

 Proof:

 Distance between two points

![Image 20: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-18.png?resize=333%2C344&ssl=1)

 ∴ AB = BC = AC … [From (i), (ii) and (iii)]

 ∴ ∆ABC is an equilateral triangle.

 ∴ Points A, B and C are the vertices of an equilateral triangle.

**Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Chapter 5 Coordinate Geometry Intext Questions and Activities**

Question 1.

 In the figure, seg AB || Y-axis and seg CB || X-axis. Co-ordinates of points A and C are given. To find AC, fill in the boxes given below. (Textbook pa. no. 102)

![Image 21: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.1 19](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.1-19.jpg?resize=274%2C288&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 In ∆ABC, ∠B = 900

 ∴ (AB)2 + (BC)2 = [(Ac)2 …(i) … [Pythagoras theorem]

 seg CB || X-axis

 ∴ y co-ordinate of B = 2

 seg BA || Y-axis

 ∴ x co-ordinate of B = 2

 ∴ co-ordinate of B is (2, 2) = (x 1,y 1)

 co-ordinate of A is (2, 3) = (x 2, Y 2)

 Since, AB || to Y-axis,

 d(A, B) = Y 2 – Y 1

 d(A,B) = 3 – 2 = 1

 co-ordinate of C is (-2,2) = (x 1,y 1)

 co-ordinate of B is (2, 2) = (x 2, y 2)

 Since, BC || to X-axis,

 d(B, C) = x 2 – x 1

 d(B,C) = 2 – -2 = 4

 ∴ AC 2 = 12 + 42 …[From (i)]

 = 1 + 16 = 17

 ∴ AC = 17−−√ units …[Taking square root of both sides]

notes.title: Practice Set 5.2 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 5.2 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 5.2 Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 Find the co-ordinates of point P if P divides the line segment joining the points A (-1, 7) and B (4, -3) in the ratio 2:3.

 Solution:

 Let the co-ordinates of point P be (x, y) and A (x 1, y 1) B (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 Here, x 1 = -1, y 1 = 7, x 2 = 4, y 2 = -3, m = 2, n = 3

 ∴ By section formula,

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-1.png?resize=293%2C204&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of point P are (1,3).

Question 2.

 In each of the following examples find the co-ordinates of point A which divides segment PQ in the ratio a : b.

 i. P (-3, 7), Q (1, -4), a : b = 2 : 1

 ii. P (-2, -5), Q (4, 3), a : b = 3 : 4

 iii. P (2, 6), Q (-4, 1), a : b = 1 : 2

 Solution:

 Let the co-ordinates of point A be (x, y).

 i. Let P (x 1, y 1), Q (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 Here, x 1 = -3, y 1 = 7, x 2 = 1, y 2 = -4, a = 2, b = 1

 ∴ By section formula,

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-2.png?resize=247%2C181&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of point A are (\frac { -1 }{ 3 } ,\frac { -1 }{ 3 } ).

ii. Let P (x 1,y 1), Q (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 Here, x 1 = -2, y 1 = -5, x 2 = 4, y 2 = 3, a = 3, b = 4

 By section formula,

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-3.png?resize=250%2C223&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of point A are (\frac { 4 }{ 7 } ,\frac { -11 }{ 7 } )

iii. Let P (x 1, y 1), Q (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 Here,x 1 = 2,y 1 = 6, x 2 = -4, y 2 = 1, a = 1,b = 2

 ∴ By section formula,

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-4.png?resize=217%2C245&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of point A are (0,\frac { 13 }{ 3 } )

Question 3.

 Find the ratio in which point T (-1, 6) divides the line segment joining the points P (-3,10) and Q (6, -8).

 Solution:

 Let P (x 1, y 1), Q (x 2, y 2) and T (x, y) be the given points.

 Here, x 1 = -3, y 1 = 10, x 2 = 6, y 2 = -8, x = -1, y = 6

 ∴ By section formula,

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-5.png?resize=215%2C217&ssl=1)

 ∴ Point T divides seg PQ in the ratio 2 : 7.

Question 4.

 Point P is the centre of the circle and AB is a diameter. Find the co-ordinates of point B if co-ordinates of point A and P are (2, -3) and (-2,0) respectively.

 Solution:

 Let A (x 1, y 1), B (x 2, y 2) and P (x, y) be the given points.

 Here, x 1 = 2, y 1 =-3,

 x = -2, y = 0

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-6.png?resize=117%2C146&ssl=1)

 Point P is the midpoint of seg AB.

 ∴ By midpoint formula,

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-7.png?resize=185%2C267&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of point B are (-6,3).

Question 5.

 Find the ratio in which point P (k, 7) divides the segment joining A (8, 9) and B (1,2). Also find k.

 Solution:

 Let A (x 1, y 1), B (x 2, y 2) and P (x, y) be the given points.

 Here, x 1 = 8, y 1 = 9, x 2 = 1, y 2 = 2, x = k, y = 7

 ∴ By section formula,

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-8.png?resize=203%2C396&ssl=1)

 ∴ Point P divides seg AB in the ratio 2 : 5, and the value of k is 6.

Question 6.

 Find the co-ordinates of midpoint of the segment joining the points (22, 20) and (0,16).

 Solution:

 Let A (x 1, y 1) = A (22, 20),

 B (x 2,y 2) = B (0, 16)

 Let the co-ordinates of the midpoint be P (x,y).

 ∴ By midpoint formula,

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-9.png?resize=234%2C88&ssl=1)

 The co-ordinates of the midpoint of the segment joining (22, 20) and (0, 16) are (11,18).

Question 7.

 Find the centroids of the triangles whose vertices are given below.

 i. (-7, 6), (2,-2), (8, 5)

 ii. (3, -5), (4, 3), (11,-4)

 iii. (4, 7), (8, 4), (7, 11)

 Solution:

 i. Let A (x 1, y 1) = A (-7, 6),

 B (x 2, y 2) = B (2, -2),

 C (x 3, y 3) = C(8, 5)

 ∴ By centroid formula,

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-10.png?resize=220%2C177&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the centroid are (1,3).

ii. Let A (x 1 y 1) = A (3, -5),

 B (x 2, y 2) = B (4, 3),

 C(x 3, y 3) = C(11,-4)

 ∴ By centroid formula,

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-11.png?resize=216%2C173&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the centroid are (6, -2).

iii. Let A (x 1, y 1) = A (4, 7),

 B (x 2, y 2) = B (8,4),

 C (x 3, y 3) = C(7,11)

 ∴ By centroid formula,

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-12.png?resize=196%2C173&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the centroid are (\frac { 19 }{ 3 } ,\frac { 22 }{ 3 } )

Question 8.

 In ∆ABC, G (-4, -7) is the centroid. If A (-14, -19) and B (3, 5), then find the co-ordinates of C.

 Solution:

 G (x, y) = G (-4, -7),

 A (x 1, y 1) = A (-14, -19),

 B(x 2, y 2) = B(3,5)

 Let the co-ordinates of point C be (x 3, y 3).

 G is the centroid.

 By centroid formula,

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-13.png?resize=216%2C302&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of point C are (-1, – 7).

Question 9.

 A (h, -6), B (2, 3) and C (-6, k) are the co-ordinates of vertices of a triangle whose centroid is G (1,5). Find h and k.

 Solution:

 A(x 1,y 1) = A(h, -6),

 B (x 2, y 2) = B(2, 3),

 C (x 3, y 3) = C (-6, k)

 ∴ centroid G (x, y) = G (1, 5)

 G is the centroid.

 By centroid formula,

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-14.png?resize=209%2C106&ssl=1)

 ∴ 3 = h – 4

 ∴ h = 3 + 4

 ∴ h = 7

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-15.png?resize=180%2C87&ssl=1)

 ∴ 15 = -3 + k

 ∴ k = 15 + 3

 ∴ k = 18

 ∴ h = 7 and k = 18

Question 10.

 Find the co-ordinates of the points of trisection of the line segment AB with A (2,7) and B (-4, -8).

 Solution:

 A (2, 7), B H,-8)

 Suppose the points P and Q trisect seg AB.

 ∴ AP = PQ = QB

![Image 18: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 16](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-16.png?resize=373%2C172&ssl=1)

 ∴ Point P divides seg AB in the ratio 1:2.

 ∴ By section formula,

![Image 19: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 17](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-17.png?resize=275%2C262&ssl=1)

 Co-ordinates of P are (0, 2).

 Point Q is the midpoint of PB.

 By midpoint formula,

![Image 20: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-18.png?resize=297%2C214&ssl=1)

 Co-ordinates of Q are (-2, -3).

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the points of trisection seg AB are (0,2) and (-2, -3).

Question 11.

 If A (-14, -10), B (6, -2) are given, find the co-ordinates of the points which divide segment AB into four equal parts.

 Solution:

 Let the points C, D and E divide seg AB in four equal parts.

![Image 21: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 19](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-19.png?resize=398%2C50&ssl=1)

 Point D is the midpoint of seg AB.

 ∴ By midpoint formula,

![Image 22: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 20](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-20.png?resize=252%2C274&ssl=1)

 ∴ Co-ordinates of D are (-4, -6).

 Point C is the midpoint of seg AD.

 ∴ By midpoint formula,

![Image 23: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 21](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-21.png?resize=262%2C268&ssl=1)

 ∴ Co-ordinates of C are (-9, -8).

 Point E is the midpoint of seg DB.

 ∴ By midpoint formula,

![Image 24: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 22](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-22.png?resize=256%2C133&ssl=1)

![Image 25: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 23](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-23.png?resize=248%2C126&ssl=1)

 ∴ Co-ordinates of E are (1,-4).

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the points dividing seg AB in four equal parts are C(-9, -8), D(-4, -6) and E(1, – 4).

Question 12.

 If A (20, 10), B (0, 20) are given, find the co-ordinates of the points which divide segment AB into five congruent parts.

 Solution:

 Suppose the points C, D, E and F divide seg AB in five congruent parts.

 ∴ AC = CD = DE = EF = FB

![Image 26: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 24](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-24.png?resize=406%2C494&ssl=1)

 ∴ co-ordinates of C are (16, 12).

 E is the midpoint of seg CB.

 By midpoint formula,

![Image 27: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 25](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-25.png?resize=306%2C174&ssl=1)

 ∴ co-ordinates of E are (8, 16).

 D is the midpoint of seg CE.

![Image 28: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 26](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-26.png?resize=335%2C385&ssl=1)

 ∴ co-ordinates of F are (4, 18).

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the points dividing seg AB in five congruent parts are C (16, 12), D (12, 14), E (8, 16) and F (4, 18).

**Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Intext Questions and Activities**

Question 1.

 A (15, 5), B (9, 20) and A-P-B. Find the ratio in which point P (11, 15) divides segment AB. Find the ratio using x and y co-ordinates. Write the conclusion. (Textbook pg. no. 113)

 Solution:

 Suppose point P (11,15) divides segment AB in the ratio m : n.

 By section formula,

![Image 29: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 27](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-27.png?resize=276%2C369&ssl=1)

 ∴ Point P divides seg AB in the ratio 2 : 1.

 The ratio obtained by using x and y co-ordinates is the same.

Question 2.

 External division: (Textbook pg. no. 115)

 Suppose point R divides seg PQ externally in the ratio 3:1.

![Image 30: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.2 28](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.2-28.png?resize=344%2C116&ssl=1)

 Let the common multiple be k.

 Let PR = 3k and QR = k

 Now, PR = PQ + QR … [P – Q – R]

 ∴ 3k = PQ + k

 ∴ \frac { PQ }{ QR }  = \frac { 2k }{ k }  = \frac { 2 }{ 1 }

 ∴ Point Q divides seg PR in the ratio 2 : 1 internally.

 Thus, we can find the co-ordinates of point R, when co-ordinates of points P and Q are given.

notes.title: Practice Set 5.3 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 5.3 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 5.3 Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Practice Set 5.3 Geometry Class 10 Question 1. Angles made by the line with the positive direction of X-axis are given. Find the slope of these lines.

 i. 45°

 ii. 60°

 iii. 90°

 Solution:

 i. Angle made with the positive direction of

 X-axis (θ) = 45°

 Slope of the line (m) = tan θ

 ∴ m = tan 45° = 1

 ∴ The slope of the line is 1.

ii. Angle made with the positive direction of X-axis (θ) = 60°

 Slope of the line (m) = tan θ

 ∴ m = tan 60° = 3–√

 ∴ The slope of the line is 3–√.

iii. Angle made with the positive direction of

 X-axis (θ) = 90°

 Slope of the line (m) = tan θ

 ∴ m = tan 90°

 But, the value of tan 90° is not defined.

 ∴ The slope of the line cannot be determined.

Practice Set 5.3 Geometry Question 2. Find the slopes of the lines passing through the given points.

 i. A (2, 3), B (4, 7)

 ii. P(-3, 1), Q (5, -2)

 iii. C (5, -2), D (7, 3)

 iv. L (-2, -3), M (-6, -8)

 v. E (-4, -2), F (6, 3)

 vi. T (0, -3), s (0,4)

 Solution:

 i. A (x 1, y 1) = A (2, 3) and B (x 2, y 2) = B (4, 7)

 Here, x 1 = 2, x 2 = 4, y 1 = 3, y 2 = 7

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-1.png?resize=251%2C89&ssl=1)

 ∴ The slope of line AB is 2.

ii. P (x 1, y 1) = P (-3, 1) and Q (x 2, y 2) = Q (5, -2)

 Here, x 1 = -3, x 2 = 5, y 1 = 1, y 2 = -2

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-2.png?resize=303%2C93&ssl=1)

 ∴ The slope of line PQ is −3 8

iii. C (x 1, y 1) = C (5, -2) and D (x 2, y 2) = D (7, 3)

 Here, x 1 = 5, x 2 = 7, y 1 = -2, y 2 = 3

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-3.png?resize=296%2C90&ssl=1)

 ∴ The slope of line CD is 5 2

iv. L (x 1, y 1) = L (-2, -3) and M (x 2,y 2) = M (-6, -8)

 Here, x 1 = -2, x 2 = – 6, y 1 = – 3, y 2 = – 8

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-4.png?resize=287%2C139&ssl=1)

 ∴ The slope of line LM is 5 4

v. E (x 1, y 1) = E (-4, -2) and F (x 2, y 2) = F (6, 3)

 Here,x 1 = -4, x 2 = 6, y 1 = -2, y 2 = 3

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-5.png?resize=269%2C137&ssl=1)

 ∴ The slope of line EF is 1 2.

vi. T (x 1, y 1) = T (0, -3) and S (x 2, y 2) = S (0, 4)

 Here, x 1 = 0, x 2 = 0, y 1 = -3, y 2 = 4

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-6.png?resize=304%2C111&ssl=1)

 ∴ The slope of line TS cannot be determined.

5.3.5 Practice Question 3. Determine whether the following points are collinear.

 i. A (-1, -1), B (0, 1), C (1, 3)

 ii. D (- 2, -3), E (1, 0), F (2, 1)

 iii. L (2, 5), M (3, 3), N (5, 1)

 iv. P (2, -5), Q (1, -3), R (-2, 3)

 v. R (1, -4), S (-2, 2), T (-3,4)

 vi. A(-4,4),K[-2,5 2], N (4,-2)

 Solution:

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-7.png?resize=356%2C68&ssl=1)

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-8.png?resize=294%2C47&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line AB = slope of line BC

 ∴ line AB || line BC

 Also, point B is common to both the lines.

 ∴ Both lines are the same.

 ∴ Points A, B and C are collinear.

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-9.png?resize=358%2C137&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line DE = slope of line EF

 ∴ line DE || line EF

 Also, point E is common to both the lines.

 ∴ Both lines are the same.

 ∴ Points D, E and F are collinear.

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-10.png?resize=378%2C93&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line LM ≠ slope of line MN

 ∴ Points L, M and N are not collinear.

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 11a](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-11a.png?resize=372%2C183&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line PQ = slope of line QR

 ∴ line PQ || line QR

 Also, point Q is common to both the lines.

 ∴ Both lines are the same.

 ∴ Points P, Q and R are collinear.

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-12.png?resize=376%2C184&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line RS = slope of line ST

 ∴ line RS || line ST

 Also, point S is common to both the lines.

 ∴ Both lines are the same.

 ∴ Points R, S and T are collinear.

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-13.png?resize=392%2C317&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line AK = slope of line KN

 ∴ line AK || line KN

 Also, point K is common to both the lines.

 ∴ Both lines are the same.

 ∴ Points A, K and N are collinear.

Practice Set 5.3 Geometry 9th Standard Question 4. If A (1, -1), B (0,4), C (-5,3) are vertices of a triangle, then find the slope of each side.

 Solution:

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-14.png?resize=296%2C223&ssl=1)

 ∴ The slopes of the sides AB, BC and AC are -5, 1 5 and −2 3 respectively.

Geometry 5.3 Question 5. Show that A (-4, -7), B (-1, 2), C (8, 5) and D (5, -4) are the vertices of a parallelogram.

 Proof:

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-15.png?resize=319%2C234&ssl=1)

![Image 18: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 16](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-16.png?resize=323%2C150&ssl=1)

 ∴ Slope of side AB = Slope of side CD … [From (i) and (iii)]

 ∴ side AB || side CD

 Slope of side BC = Slope of side AD … [From (ii) and (iv)]

 ∴ side BC || side AD

 Both the pairs of opposite sides of ꠸ABCD are parallel.

 ꠸ABCD is a parallelogram.

 Points A(-4, -7), B(-1, 2), C(8, 5) and D(5, -4) are the vertices of a parallelogram.

Question 6.

 Find k, if R (1, -1), S (-2, k) and slope of line RS is -2.

 Solution:

 R(x 1, y 1) = R (1, -1), S (x 2, y 2) = S (-2, k)

 Here, x 1 = 1, x 2 = -2, y 1 = -1, y 2 = k

![Image 19: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 17](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-17.png?resize=320%2C51&ssl=1)

 But, slope of line RS is -2. … [Given]

 ∴ -2 = k+1−3

 ∴ k + 1 = 6

 ∴ k = 6 – 1

 ∴ k = 5

5.3 Class 10 Question 7. Find k, if B (k, -5), C (1, 2) and slope of the line is 7.

 Solution:

 B(x 1, y 1) = B (k, -5), C (x 2, y 2) = C (1, 2)

 Here, x 1 = k, x 2 = 1, y 1 = -5, y 2 = 2

![Image 20: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-18.png?resize=290%2C98&ssl=1)

 But, slope of line BC is 7. …[Given]

 ∴ 7 = 7 1−k

 ∴ 7(1 – k) = 7

 ∴ 1 – k = 7 7

 ∴ 1 – k = 1

 ∴ k = 0

Question 8.

 Find k, if PQ || RS and P (2, 4), Q (3, 6), R (3,1), S (5, k).

 Solution:

![Image 21: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Practice Set 5.3 19](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Practice-Set-5.3-19.png?resize=309%2C93&ssl=1)

 But, line PQ || line RS … [Given]

 ∴ Slope of line PQ = Slope of line RS

 ∴ 2 = k−1 2

 ∴ 4 = k – 1

 ∴ k = 4 + 1

 ∴ k = 5

notes.title: Practice Set 5 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Problem Set 5 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Problem Set 5 Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 Fill in the blanks using correct alternatives.

i. Seg AB is parallel to Y-axis and co-ordinates of point A are (1, 3), then co-ordinates of point B can be _______.

 (A) (3,1)

 (B) (5,3)

 (C) (3,0)

 (D) (1,-3)

 Answer: (D)

 Since, seg AB || Y-axis.

 ∴ x co-ordinate of all points on seg AB

 will be the same,

 x co-ordinate of A (1, 3) = 1

 x co-ordinate of B (1, – 3) = 1

 ∴ Option (D) is correct.

ii. Out of the following, point lies to the right of the origin on X-axis.

 (A) (-2,0)

 (B) (0,2)

 (C) (2,3)

 (D) (2,0)

 Answer: (D)

iii. Distance of point (-3, 4) from the origin is _________.

 (A) 7

 (B) 1

 (C) 5

 (D) -5

 Answer: (C)

 Distance of (-3, 4) from origin

=(−3)2+(4)2−−−−−−−−−−√=9+16−−−−−√=25−−√=5

iv. A line makes an angle of 30° with the positive direction of X-axis. So the slope of the line is ________.

 (A) 1 2

 (B) 3√2

 (C) 1 3√

 (D) 3–√

 Answer: (C)

Question 2.

 Determine whether the given points are collinear.

 i. A (0, 2), B (1, -0.5), C (2, -3)

 ii. P(1,2), Q(2,8 5),R(3,6 5)

 iii L (1, 2), M (5, 3), N (8, 6)

 Solution:

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-1.png?resize=329%2C230&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line AB = slope of line BC

 ∴ line AB || line BC

 Also, point B is common to both the lines.

 ∴ Both lines are the same.

 ∴ Points A, B and C are collinear.

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-2.png?resize=344%2C222&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line PQ = slope of line QR

 ∴ line PQ || line QR

 Also, point Q is common to both the lines.

 ∴ Both lines are the same.

 ∴ Points P, Q and R are collinear.

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-3.png?resize=320%2C186&ssl=1)

 ∴ slope of line LM ≠ slope of line MN

 ∴ Points L, M and N are not collinear.

 [Note: Students can solve the above problems by using distance formula.]

Question 3.

 Find the co-ordinates of the midpoint of the line segment joining P (0,6) and Q (12,20).

 Solution:

 P(x 1,y 1) = P (0, 6), Q(x 2, y 2) = Q (12, 20)

 Here, x 1 = 0, y 1 = 6, x 2 = 12, y 2 = 20

 ∴ Co-ordinates of the midpoint of seg PQ

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-4.png?resize=183%2C166&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the midpoint of seg PQ are (6,13).

Question 4.

 Find the ratio in which the line segment joining the points A (3, 8) and B (-9, 3) is divided by the Y-axis.

 Solution:

 Let C be a point on Y-axis which divides seg AB in the ratio m : n.

 Point C lies on the Y-axis

 ∴ its x co-ordinate is 0.

 Let C = (0, y)

 Here A (x 1,y 1) = A(3, 8)

 B (x 2, y 2) = B (-9, 3)

 ∴ By section formula,

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-5.png?resize=183%2C198&ssl=1)

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-6.png?resize=189%2C246&ssl=1)

 ∴ Y-axis divides the seg AB in the ratio 1 : 3.

Question 5.

 Find the point on X-axis which is equidistant from P (2, -5) and Q (-2,9).

 Solution:

 Let point R be on the X-axis which is equidistant from points P and Q.

 Point R lies on X-axis.

 ∴ its y co-ordinate is 0.

 Let R = (x, 0)

 R is equidistant from points P and Q.

 ∴ PR = QR

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-7.jpg?resize=384%2C57&ssl=1)

 ∴ (x – 2)2 + [0 – (-5)]2 = [x – (- 2)]2 + (0 – 9)2 …[Squaring both sides]

 ∴ (x – 2)2 + (5)2 = (x + 2)2 + (-9)2

 ∴ 4 – 4x + x 2 + 25 = 4 + 4x + x 2 + 81

 ∴ – 8x = 56

 ∴ x = -7

 ∴ The point on X-axis which is equidistant from points P and Q is (-7,0).

Question 6.

 Find the distances between the following points.

 i. A (a, 0), B (0, a)

 ii. P (-6, -3), Q (-1, 9)

 iii. R (-3a, a), S (a, -2a)

 Solution:

 i. Let A (x 1, y 1) and B (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 ∴ x 1 = a, y 1 = 0, x 2 = 0, y 2 = a

 By distance formula,

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-8.png?resize=271%2C145&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(A, B) = a 2–√ units

ii. Let P (x 1, y 1) and Q (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 ∴ x 1 = -6, y 1 = -3, x 2 = -1, y 2 = 9

 By distance formula,

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-9.png?resize=248%2C178&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(P, Q) = 13 units

iii. Let R (x 1, y 1) and S (x 2, y 2) be the given points.

 ∴ x 1 = -3a, y 1 = a, x 2 = a, y 2 = -2a

 By distance formula,

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-10.png?resize=274%2C178&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(R, S) = 5a units

Question 7.

 Find the co-ordinates of the circumcentre of a triangle whose vertices are (-3,1), (0, -2) and (1,3).

 Solution:

 Let A (-3, 1), B (0, -2) and C (1, 3) be the vertices of the triangle.

 Suppose O (h, k) is the circumcentre of ∆ABC.

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-11.png?resize=382%2C295&ssl=1)

 ∴ (h + 3)2 + (k – 1)2 = h 2 + (k + 2)2

 ∴ h 2 + 6h + 9 + k 2 – 2k + 1 = h 2 + k 2 + 4k + 4

 ∴ 6h – 2k + 10 = 4k + 4

 ∴ 6h – 2k – 4k = 4 – 10

 ∴ 6h – 6k = – 6

 ∴ h – k = -1 ,..(i)[Dividing both sides by 6]

 OB = OC …[Radii of the same circle]

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-12.png?resize=386%2C93&ssl=1)

 ∴ h 2 + (k + 2)2 = (h – 1)2 + (k – 3)2

 ∴ h 2 + k 2 + 4k + 4 = h 2 – 2h + 1 + k 2 – 6k + 9

 ∴ 4k + 4 = -2h + 1 – 6k + 9

 ∴ 2h+ 10k = 6

 ∴ h + 5k = 3 …(ii)

 Subtracting equation (ii) from (i), we get

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-13.png?resize=379%2C281&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the circumcentre of the triangle are (−1 3,2 3)

Question 8.

 In the following examples, can the segment joining the given points form a triangle? If triangle is formed, state the type of the triangle considering sides of the triangle.

 i. L (6, 4), M (-5, -3), N (-6, 8)

 ii. P (-2, -6), Q (-4, -2), R (-5, 0)

 iii. A(2–√,2–√),B(-2–√,-2–√),C(6–√,6–√)

 Solution:

 i. By distance formula,

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-14.png?resize=319%2C514&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(M, N) + d (L, N) > d (L, M)

 ∴ Points L, M, N are non collinear points.

 We can construct a triangle through 3 non collinear points.

 ∴ The segment joining the given points form a triangle.

 Since MN ≠ LN ≠ LM

 ∴ ∆LMN is a scalene triangle.

 ∴ The segments joining the points L, M and N will form a scalene triangle.

ii. By distance formula,

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-15.png?resize=291%2C131&ssl=1)

![Image 18: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 16](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-16.png?resize=341%2C462&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(P, Q) + d(Q, R) = d (P, R) …[From (iii)]

 ∴ Points P, Q, R are collinear points.

 We cannot construct a triangle through 3 collinear points.

 ∴ The segments joining the points P, Q and R will not form a triangle.

iii. By distance formula,

![Image 19: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 17](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-17.png?resize=345%2C524&ssl=1)

 ∴ d(A, B) + d(B, C) + d(A, C) … [From (iii)]

 ∴ Points A, B, C are non collinear points.

 We can construct a triangle through 3 non collinear points.

 ∴ The segment joining the given points form a triangle.

 Since, AB = BC = AC

 ∴ ∆ABC is an equilateral triangle.

 ∴ The segments joining the points A, B and C will form an equilateral triangle.

Question 9.

 Find k, if the line passing through points P (-12, -3) and Q (4, k) has slope 1 2.

 Solution:

 P(x 1,y 1) = P(-12,-3),

 Q(X 2,T 2) = Q(4, k)

 Here, x 1 = -12, x 2 = 4, y 1 = -3, y 2 = k

![Image 20: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-18.png?resize=278%2C192&ssl=1)

 But, slope of line PQ (m) is 1 2 ….[Given]

 ∴ 1 2 = k+3 16

 ∴ 16 2 = k + 3

 ∴ 8 = k + 3

 ∴ k = 5

 The value of k is 5.

Question 10.

 Show that the line joining the points A (4,8) and B (5, 5) is parallel to the line joining the points C (2, 4) and D (1 ,7).

 Proof:

![Image 21: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 19](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-19.png?resize=283%2C97&ssl=1)

 ∴ Slope of line AB = Slope of line CD

 Parallel lines have equal slope.

 ∴ line AB || line CD

Question 11.

 Show that points P (1, -2), Q (5, 2), R (3, -1), S (-1, -5) are the vertices of a parallelogram.

 Proof:

 By distance formula,

![Image 22: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 20](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-20.png?resize=266%2C540&ssl=1)

 In ꠸PQRS,

 PQ = RS … [From (i) and (iii)]

 QR = PS … [From (ii) and (iv)]

 ∴ ꠸ PQRS is a parallelogram.

 [A quadrilateral is a parallelogram, if both the pairs of its opposite sides are congruent]

 ∴ Points P, Q, R and S are the vertices of a parallelogram.

Question 12.

 Show that the ꠸PQRS formed by P (2, 1), Q (-1, 3), R (-5, -3) and S (-2, -5) is a rectangle.

 Proof:

 By distance formula,

![Image 23: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 21](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-21.png?resize=298%2C223&ssl=1)

![Image 24: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 22](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-22.png?resize=323%2C212&ssl=1)

 In ꠸PQRS,

 PQ = RS …[From (i) and (iii)]

 QR = PS …[From (ii) and (iv)]

 ꠸PQRS is a parallelogram.

 [A quadrilateral is a parallelogram, if both the pairs of its opposite sides are congruent]

![Image 25: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 23](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-23.png?resize=306%2C222&ssl=1)

 In parallelogram PQRS,

 PR = QS … [From (v) and (vi)]

 ∴ ꠸PQRS is a rectangle.

 [A parallelogram is a rectangle if its diagonals are equal]

Question 13.

 Find the lengths of the medians of a triangle whose vertices are A (-1, 1), B (5, -3) and C (3,5).

 Solution:

![Image 26: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 24](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-24.png?resize=269%2C140&ssl=1)

 Suppose AD, BE and CF are the medians.

 ∴ Points D, E and F are the midpoints of sides BC, AC and AB respectively.

 ∴ By midpoint formula,

![Image 27: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 25](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-25.png?resize=282%2C163&ssl=1)

![Image 28: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 26](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-26.png?resize=274%2C513&ssl=1)

 ∴ The lengths of the medians of the triangle 5 units, 2 13−−√ units and 37−−√ units.

Question 14.

 Find the co-ordinates of centroid of the triangle if points D (-7, 6), E (8, 5) and F (2, -2) are the mid points of the sides of that triangle.

 Solution:

![Image 29: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 27](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-27.png?resize=302%2C162&ssl=1)

 Suppose A (x 1, y 1), B (x 2, y 2) and C (x 3, y 3) are the vertices of the triangle.

 D (-7, 6), E (8, 5) and F (2, -2) are the midpoints of sides BC, AC and AB respectively.

 Let G be the centroid of ∆ABC.

 D is the midpoint of seg BC.

 By midpoint formula,

![Image 30: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 28](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-28.png?resize=329%2C182&ssl=1)

 E is the midpoint of seg AC.

 By midpoint formula,

![Image 31: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 29](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-29.png?resize=322%2C413&ssl=1)

 Adding (i), (iii) and (v),

 x 2 + x 3 + x 1 + x 3 + x 1 + x 2 = -14 + 16 + 4

 ∴ 2x 1 + 2x 2 + 2x 3 = 6

 ∴ x 1 + x 2 + x 3 = 3 …(vii)

 Adding (ii), (iv) and (vi),

 y 2 + y 3 + y 1 + y 3 + y 1 +y 2 = 12 + 10 – 4

 ∴ 2y 1 + 2y 2 + 2y 3 = 18

 ∴ y 1 + y 2 + y 3 = 9 …(viii)

 G is the centroid of ∆ABC.

 By centroid formula,

![Image 32: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 30](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-30.png?resize=336%2C142&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the centroid of the triangle are (1,3).

Question 15.

 Show that A (4, -1), B (6, 0), C (7, -2) and D (5, -3) are vertices of a square.

 Proof:

 By distance formula,

![Image 33: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 31](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-31.png?resize=318%2C196&ssl=1)

![Image 34: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 32](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-32.png?resize=381%2C596&ssl=1)

 ∴ □ABCD is a square.

 [A rhombus is a square if its diagonals are equal]

Question 16.

 Find the co-ordinates of circumcentre and radius of circumcircle of AABC if A (7, 1), B (3,5) and C (2,0) are given.

 Solution:

 Suppose, O (h, k) is the circumcentre of ∆ABC

![Image 35: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 33](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-33.png?resize=382%2C366&ssl=1)

![Image 36: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 34](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-34.png?resize=379%2C117&ssl=1)

 ∴ h 2 – 6h + 9 + k 2 – 10k + 25 = h 2 – 4h + 4 + k 2

 ∴ 2h + 10k = 30

 ∴ h + 5k = 15 … (ii)[Dividing both sides by 2]

 Multiplying equation (i) by 5, we get

 25h + 5k = 115 …(iii)

 Subtracting equation (ii) from (iii), we get

![Image 37: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 35](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-35.png?resize=313%2C121&ssl=1)

 Substituting the value of h in equation (i), we get

![Image 38: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 36](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-36.png?resize=363%2C463&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the circumcentre of the triangle are (25 6,13 6) and radius of circumcircle is 13 2√6 units.

Question 17.

 Given A (4, -3), B (8, 5). Find the co-ordinates of the point that divides segment AB in the ratio 3:1.

 Solution:

 Suppose point C divides seg AB in the ratio 3:1.

 Here; A(x 1, y 1) = A (4, -3)

 B (x 2, y 2) = B (8, 5)

 By section formula,

![Image 39: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 37](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-37.png?resize=318%2C326&ssl=1)

 ∴ The co-ordinates of point dividing seg AB in ratio 3 : 1 are (7, 3).

Question 18.

 Find the type of the quadrilateral if points A (-4, -2), B (-3, -7), C (3, -2) and D (2, 3) are joined serially.

 Solution:

![Image 40: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 38](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-38.png?resize=311%2C433&ssl=1)

 Slope of AB = slope of CD

 ∴ line AB || line CD

 slope of BC = slope of AD

 ∴ line BC || line AD

 Both the pairs of opposite sides of ∆ABCD are parallel.

 ∴ ꠸ ABCD is a parallelogram.

 ∴ The quadrilateral formed by joining the points A, B, C and D is a parallelogram.

Question 19.

 The line segment AB is divided into five congruent parts at P, Q, R and S such that A-P-Q-R-S-B. If point Q (12, 14) and S (4, 18) are given, find the co-ordinates of A, P, R, B.

 Solution:

![Image 41: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 39](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-39.png?resize=343%2C45&ssl=1)

 Points P, Q, R and S divide seg AB in five congruent parts.

 Let A (x 1, y 1), B (x 2, y 2), P (x 3, y 3) and

 R (x 4, y 4) be the given points.

 Point R is the midpoint of seg QS.

 By midpoint formula,

 x co-ordinate of R = 12+4 2 = 16 2 = 8

 y co-ordinate of R = 14+18 2 = 32 2 = 16

 ∴ co-ordinates of R are (8, 16).

 Point Q is the midpoint of seg PR.

 By midpoint formula,

![Image 42: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 40](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-40.png?resize=255%2C231&ssl=1)

 ∴ 28 = y 3 + 16

 ∴ y 3 = 12

 ∴ P(x 3,y 3) = (16, 12)

 ∴ co-ordinates of P are (16, 12).

 Point P is the midpoint of seg AQ.

 By midpoint formula,

![Image 43: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 41](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-41.png?resize=286%2C307&ssl=1)

 ∴ co-ordinates of A are (20, 10).

 Point S is the midpoint of seg RB.

 By midpoint formula,

![Image 44: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 42](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-42.png?resize=286%2C217&ssl=1)

 ∴ 36 = y 2 + 16

 ∴ y 2 = 20

 ∴ B(x 2, y 2) = (0, 20)

 ∴ co-ordinates of B are (0, 20).

 ∴ The co-ordinates of points A, P, R and B are (20, 10), (16, 12), (8, 16) and (0, 20) respectively.

Question 20.

 Find the co-ordinates of the centre of the circle passing through the points P (6, -6), Q (3, -7) and R (3,3).

 Solution:

 Suppose O (h, k) is the centre of the circle passing through the points P, Q and R.

![Image 45: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 43](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-43.png?resize=384%2C233&ssl=1)

 ∴ (h – 6)2 + (k + 6)2 = (h – 3)2 + (k + 7)2

 ∴ h 2 – 12h + 36 + k 2 + 12k + 36

 = h 2 – 6h + 9 + k 2 + 14k + 49

 ∴ 6h + 2k = 14

 ∴ 3h + k = 7 …(i)[Dividing both sides by 2]

 OP = OR …[Radii of the same circle]

![Image 46: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 44](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-44.png?resize=388%2C109&ssl=1)

 ∴ (h – 6)2 + (k + 6)2 = (h – 3)2 + (k – 3)2

 ∴ h 2 – 12h + 36 + k 2 + 12k + 36

 = h 2 – 6h + 9 + k 2 – 6k + 9

 ∴ 6h – 18k = 54

 ∴ 3h – 9k = 27 …(ii)[Dividing both sides by 2]

 Subtracting equation (ii) from (i), we get

![Image 47: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 45](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-45.png?resize=217%2C142&ssl=1)

 Substituting the value of k in equation (i), we get

 3h – 2 = 7

 ∴ 3h = 9

 ∴ h = 9 3 = 3

 ∴ The co-ordinates of the centre of the circle are (3, -2).

Question 21.

 Find the possible pairs of co-ordinates of the fourth vertex D of the parallelogram, if three of its vertices are A (5, 6), B (1, -2) and C (3, -2).

 Solution:

![Image 48: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 46](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-46.png?resize=360%2C207&ssl=1)

 Let the points A (5, 6), B (1, -2) and C (3, -2) be the three vertices of a parallelogram.

 The fourth vertex can be point D or point Di or point D 2 as shown in the figure.

 Let D(x 1,y 1), D, (x 2, y 2) and D 2 (x 3,y 3).

 Consider the parallelogram ACBD.

 The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

 ∴ midpoint of DC = midpoint of AB

![Image 49: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 47](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-47.png?resize=295%2C101&ssl=1)

![Image 50: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 48](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-48.png?resize=287%2C97&ssl=1)

 Co-ordinates of point D(x 1, y 1) are (3, 6).

 Consider the parallelogram ABD 1 C.

 The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

 ∴ midpoint of AD 1 = midpoint of BC

![Image 51: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 49](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-49.png?resize=314%2C203&ssl=1)

 ∴ Co-ordinates of D 1(x 2,y 2) are (-1,-10).

 Consider the parallelogram ABCD 2.

 The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other.

 ∴ midpoint of BD 2 = midpoint of AC

![Image 52: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 50](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-50.png?resize=305%2C198&ssl=1)

 ∴ co-ordinates of point D 2 (x 3, y 3) are (7, 6).

 ∴ The possible pairs of co-ordinates of the fourth vertex D of the parallelogram are (3, 6), (-1,-10) and (7,6).

Question 22.

 Find the slope of the diagonals of a quadrilateral with vertices A (1, 7), B (6,3), C (0, -3) and D (-3,3).

 Solution:

 Suppose ABCD is the given quadrilateral.

![Image 53: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 5 Co-ordinate Geometry Problem Set 5 51](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-5-Co-ordinate-Geometry-Problem-Set-5-51.png?resize=376%2C135&ssl=1)

 ∴ The slopes of the diagonals of the quadrilateral are 10 and 0.

notes.title: Practice Set 6.1 Geometry 10th Standard Maths Part 2 Chapter 6 Trigonometry
notes.content:
Balbharti [Maharashtra State Board Class 10 Maths Solutions](https://maharashtraboardsolutions.com/maharashtra-state-board-class-10-maths-solutions/) covers the Practice Set 6.1 Geometry 10th Class Maths Part 2 Answers Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry.

### Class 10 Maths Part 2 Practice Set 6.1 Chapter 6 Trigonometry Questions With Answers Maharashtra Board

Question 1.

 If sin θ = \frac { 7 }{ 25 } , find the values of cos θ and tan θ.

 Solution:

 sin θ = \frac { 7 }{ 25 }  … [Given]

 We know that,

 sin 2 θ + cos 2 θ = 1

![Image 3: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-1.png?resize=326%2C260&ssl=1)

 …[Taking square root of both sides] Now, tan θ = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}

![Image 4: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 2](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-2.png?resize=345%2C301&ssl=1)

 Alternate Method:

 sin θ = \frac { 7 }{ 25 }  …(i) [Given]

 Consider ∆ABC, where ∠ABC 90° and ∠ACB = θ.

 sin θ = \frac { AB }{ AC }  … (ii) [By definition]

 ∴ \frac { AB }{ AC }  = \frac { 7 }{ 25 }  … [From (i) and (ii)]

![Image 5: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-3.jpg?resize=126%2C112&ssl=1)

 LetAB = 7k and AC = 25k

 In ∆ABC, ∠B = 90°

 ∴ AB 2 + BC 2 = AC 2 … [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ (7k)2 + BC 2 = (25k)2

 ∴ 49k 2 + BC 2 = 625k 2

 ∴ BC 2 = 625k 2 – 49k 2

 ∴ BC 2 = 576k 2

 ∴ BC = 24k …[Taking square root of both sides]

![Image 6: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 3](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-3.png?resize=377%2C298&ssl=1)

Question 2.

 If tan θ = \frac { 3 }{ 4 } , find the values of sec θ and cos θ.

 Solution:

![Image 7: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 4](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-4.png?resize=384%2C530&ssl=1)

 Alternate Method:

 tan θ = \frac { 3 }{ 4 }  …(i)[Given]

 Consider ∆ABC, where ∠ABC 90° and ∠ACB = θ.

 tan θ = \frac { AB }{ BC }  … (ii) [By definition]

 ∴ \frac { AB }{ BC }  = \frac { 3 }{ 4 }  … [From (i) and (ii)]

![Image 8: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 5](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-5-1.png?resize=135%2C90&ssl=1)

 Let AB = 3k and BC 4k

 In ∆ABC,∠B = 90°

 ∴ AB 2 + BC 2 = AC 2 …[Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ (3k)2 + (4k)2 = AC 2

 ∴ 9k 2 + 16k 2 = AC 2

 ∴ AC 2 = 25k 2

 ∴ AC = 5k …[Taking square root of both sides]

![Image 9: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 6](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-6.png?resize=349%2C295&ssl=1)

Question 3.

 If cot θ = \frac { 40 }{ 9 } , find the values of cosec θ and sin θ

 Solution:

![Image 10: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 7](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-7.png?resize=367%2C300&ssl=1)

 ..[Taking square root of both sides]

![Image 11: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 8](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-8.png?resize=288%2C197&ssl=1)

 Alternate Method:

 cot θ = \frac { 40 }{ 9 }  ….(i) [Given]

 Consider ∆ABC, where ∠ABC = 90° and

 ∠ACB = θ

 cot θ = \frac { BC }{ AB }  …(ii) [By defnition]

 ∴ \frac { BC }{ AB }  = \frac { 40 }{ 9 }  ….. [From (i) and (ii)]

 Let BC = 40k and AB = 9k

![Image 12: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 9](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-9.png?resize=200%2C80&ssl=1)

 In ∆ABC, ∠B = 90°

 ∴ AB 2 + BC 2 = AC 2 … [Pythagoras theorem]

 ∴ (9k)2 + (40k)2 = AC 2

 ∴ 81k 2 + 1600k 2 = AC 2

 ∴ AC 2 = 1681k 2

 ∴ AC = 41k … [Taking square root of both sides]

![Image 13: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 10](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-10.png?resize=352%2C291&ssl=1)

Question 4.

 If 5 sec θ – 12 cosec θ = θ, find the values of sec θ, cos θ and sin θ.

 Solution:

 5 sec θ – 12 cosec θ = 0 …[Given]

 ∴ 5 sec θ = 12 cosec θ

![Image 14: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 11](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-11.png?resize=376%2C317&ssl=1)

![Image 15: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 12](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-12.png?resize=392%2C543&ssl=1)

Question 5.

 If tan θ = 1, then find the value of

![Image 16: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 13](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-13.png?resize=122%2C47&ssl=1)

 Solution:

 tan θ = 1 … [Given]

 We know that, tan 45° = 1

 ∴ tan θ = tan 45°

 ∴ θ = 45°

![Image 17: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 14](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-14.png?resize=268%2C414&ssl=1)

Question 6.

 Prove that:

 i. \frac{\sin ^{2} \theta}{\cos \theta}+\cos \theta=\sec \theta

 ii. cos 2 θ (1+ tan 2 θ) = 1

 iii. \sqrt{\frac{1-\sin \theta}{1+\sin \theta}}=\sec \theta-\tan \theta

 iv. (sec θ – cos θ) (cot θ + tan θ) tan θ. sec θ

 v. cot θ + tan θ cosec θ. sec θ

 vi. \frac{1}{\sec \theta-\tan \theta}=\sec \theta+\tan \theta

 vii. sin 4 θ – cos 4 θ = 1 – 2 cos 2 θ

 viii. \sec \theta+\tan \theta=\frac{\cos \theta}{1-\sin \theta}

![Image 18: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 15](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-15.png?resize=337%2C268&ssl=1)

 Proof:

 i. L.H.S. = \frac{\sin ^{2} \theta}{\cos \theta}+\cos \theta

![Image 19: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 16](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-16.png?resize=383%2C198&ssl=1)

ii. L.H.S. = cos 2 θ(1 + tan 2 θ)

 = cos 2 θ sec 2 θ …[∵ 1 + tan 2 θ = sec 2 θ]

![Image 20: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 17](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-17.png?resize=332%2C117&ssl=1)

 = 1

 = R.H.S.

 ∴ cos 2 θ (1 + tan 2 θ) = 1

![Image 21: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 18](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-18.png?resize=381%2C504&ssl=1)

iv. L.H.S. = (sec θ – cos θ) (cot θ + tan θ)

![Image 22: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 19](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-19.png?resize=361%2C293&ssl=1)

 ∴ (sec θ – cos θ) (cot θ + tan θ) = tan θ. sec θ

v. L.H.S. = cot θ + tan θ

![Image 23: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 20](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-20.png?resize=354%2C229&ssl=1)

 ∴ cot θ + tan θ = cosec θ.sec θ

![Image 24: Maharashtra Board Class 10 Maths Solutions Chapter 6 Trigonometry Practice Set 6.1 21](https://i0.wp.com/www.learncram.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/Maharashtra-Board-Class-10-Maths-Solutions-Chapter-6-Trigonometry-Practice-Set-6.1-21.png?resize=387%2C344&ssl=1)

vii. L.H.S. = sin 4 θ – cos 4 θ

 = (sin 2 θ)2 – (cos 2 θ)2

 = (sin 2 θ + cos 2 θ) (sin 2 θ – cos 2 θ)

 = (1) (sin 2 θ – cos 2 θ) ….[∵ sin 2 θ + cos 2 θ = 1]

 = sin 2 θ – cos 2 θ

 = (1 – cos 2 θ) – cos 2 θ …[θ sin 2 θ = 1 – cos 2 θ]

 = 1 – 2 cos 2 θ

 = R.H.S.

 ∴ sin 4 θ – cos 4 θ = 1 – 2 cos 2 θ

viii. L.H.S. = sec θ + tan θ
